# Certifier conformance statement

<!-- GENERATED FILE — do not edit.
     Source: documentation/compliance/certifiers/<certifier>/forms/*.yaml
     Regenerate: cd trazo-back && poetry run python manage.py certifier_conformance -->

How Trazo lines up against each certifying agent's own Organic System Plan forms, question by question. Registered: CCOF, OTCO, WSDA.
Generated from the conformance register, which is checked against the shipped OSP module
registry by `certifications/tests/test_certifier_conformance_register.py` — a question that is
renamed, removed or added without a decision fails that test rather than quietly making
this document wrong.

Statuses: **Covered** — the fact is capturable and reaches an artifact a certifier reads.
**Partial** — captured but incomplete. **Not covered** — no home in the product today.
**Out of scope** — deliberately not built, with the reason stated.

Severity is about what a reviewer at that certifier does with it: **P0** the packet is bounced or
asserts something untrue · **P1** a request for information · **P2** noticed, tolerated ·
**P3** cosmetic.

### C5 Crop Pest, Weed & Disease Management

*C5 · rev. 2023/09/14 · retrieved 2026-09-09*  
<https://tilth.org/help-center/blank-forms-all/>

**When OTCO requires it:** C1 Crop Activities Checklist — "I/We grow crops" → C2 Land History, C4 Fertility Management, C5 Pest, Weed, & Disease Management, C6 Natural Resources & Biodiversity, C9 Contamination Prevention, C12 Crop Recordkeeping. The form's own instruction: "Complete this form for all acreage to be included under certification."

**9 questions** — Covered 1 · Partial 8

| Ref | What OTCO asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1-1 | List the pests/diseases (or potential pests/diseases) that threaten your crops. | Partial | P2 | `history.PestManagementEvent.pest_species` | Neither CCOF's G5.0 nor WSDA's §F/§G/§H asks for a named list of the pests and diseases the operation actually faces (WSDA G3 asks for taxa classes — insects, rodents, birds — and is `not_covered` there on that axis), so this is a fresh OTCO ask. The fact is captured, but only per logged event: `PestManagementEvent.pest_species` names the organism observed on each scouting or control record and prints in the audit dossier. There is no plan-level statement, so an operation whose records are thin — a first-year pilot, or a season with no pest events yet — shows nothing, and even a well-logged one gives the reviewer a column of observations to deduplicate rather than the list OTCO asks for. **Fix:** Add `pests_diseases_of_concern` [textarea] on page A, ahead of `prevention_practices`, cite § 205.206; suggest the distinct `pest_species` values from logged Pest-Management events as a prefill the operator confirms (suggest→confirm — the plan is the producer's statement under § 205.201(a), not a reading of the log); compile "Pests and diseases of concern: {answer}." |
| 5.1-2 | Select all preventative practices you use for management of weeds, pests and diseases: Crop rotation / Release of beneficial insects / Nutrient management / Sanitation / Planting resistant varieties / Water management / Hand weeding / Timing of planting / Mechanical/physical methods / Inter-planting species / Cover cropping / Trap crops / Construct predator habitat / Flaming/burning / Other. | Partial | P2 | `g5_0_pest.prevention_practices` · `g5_0_pest.prevention_practices_other` · `g5_0_pest.weed_management_practices` · `g5_0_pest.weed_management_other` · `g5_0_pest.burns_crop_residue` | OTCO's list is ONE flat checklist covering weeds, pests and diseases together — the same shape as Trazo's `prevention_practices` (page A) plus `weed_management_practices` (page B) — so the structural gap both siblings carry for these same fields (CCOF: no pest-type column against a 23 × 4 matrix; WSDA: one undifferentiated list printed under three separate section headers) does not arise here, and the severity is correspondingly lower. Eleven of OTCO's fourteen named practices have a direct option: crop rotation, release of beneficial insects (`beneficial_release`), nutrient management, sanitation, resistant varieties, water management (`irrigation_management`), hand weeding, timing of planting (`spacing_timing`), mechanical/physical methods (`mechanical_cultivation`, `vertebrate_exclusion`), predator habitat (`raptor_habitat`, `beneficial_habitat`) and "Other". What is missing: "Inter-planting species" has no option anywhere on G5.0 (CCOF's own register carries it `not_covered`, restated below); "Trap crops" has no option (CCOF: `partial`, event-level only, restated below); "Cover cropping" exists on G5.0 only as `cover_crop_suppression`, framed as a weed practice, so a grower cover cropping for beneficial habitat or disease breaks has to reach for `other`. OTCO's single "Flaming/burning" box also spans two Trazo facts — `flame_weeding` (in-row thermal weed control) and `burns_crop_residue` (§ 205.203(e)(3) residue burning) — which is the honest split, since only the second carries a regulatory condition (§ 5.2 below). (5.1-2 (inter-planting species)) Same verdict as CCOF G5.0 "A (strip cropping / interplanting)": no option anywhere on G5.0 for this practice. `erosion_practices.strip_cropping` exists on G4.0, but for soil erosion control, not pest management — it does not answer this question. (5.1-2 (trap crops)) Same verdict as CCOF G5.0 "A (trap crops)" and the WSDA G4 note: not an OSP option anywhere on G5.0. The only capture is a logged Pest-Management event with `cultural_practice=trap_crop`, so an operation with no such event on file shows nothing on the static OSP snapshot. **Fix:** Add `interplanting_mixed_species` and `trap_crops` to `prevention_practices` (the same two options CCOF's G5.0 §A rows already ask for) and a general `cover_cropping` option alongside the weed-page `cover_crop_suppression`; cite § 205.206(a)(1)-(3). No matrix is needed for OTCO. Add option `interplanting_mixed_species` to `prevention_practices`; cite § 205.206(a)(1). Add option `trap_crops` to `prevention_practices`; add a prefill resolver suggesting it from cultural-practice events with `cultural_practice=trap_crop` (suggest→confirm). |
| 5.1-3 | Do you use materials for controlling weeds, pests, and/or diseases? (No / Yes, complete questions 4 and 5 below.) | Covered | — | `g5_0_pest.applies_pest_weed_disease_inputs` | — |
| 5.1-4 | Describe the conditions that must exist before you will resort to using substances for weed, pest, and/or disease control: Preventative measures described above are insufficient / Economic thresholds for pest damage are exceeded / Other. | Partial | P2 | `g5_0_pest.input_use_conditions` | Same verdict as CCOF G5.0 B2, whose two named triggers are OTCO's two: Trazo only offers a free-text `input_use_conditions` textarea; the two specific triggers are not independently selectable, so the compiled narrative cannot state that materials are used only when preventive measures are insufficient or economic thresholds are exceeded unless the operator happens to write that themselves. **Fix:** Add `input_use_triggers` [checkbox_group] {preventive_insufficient, economic_threshold, other} ahead of the textarea; cite § 205.206(e); compile "Materials are used only when: {answer}."; keep the textarea as the description. |
| 5.1-5 | Do you use plastic mulch, landscape fabric, or other physical weed barriers? (No / Yes, include manufacturer and brand name on the C11 or provide a product label.) | Partial | P2 | `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_used` | The use is captured and prints (`plastic_mulch_used`, "plastic or other synthetic mulch" — a reading that takes in landscape fabric). Trazo never makes that hand-off — a Yes here does not prompt a materials-list row, the Materials Application's category attestations have no mulch/barrier category, and the operator-entered row that could hold it (`PlanMaterialEntry`, category `production_aid` or `other`) has no label attachment (see C11 11.1 (labels or photos attached)). OTCO does not ask the season-end removal question here (§ 205.206(c)(6)), so `plastic_mulch_removal` is not cited; WSDA F4/F5 and CCOF §A carry that half. **Fix:** When `plastic_mulch_used` is true, prompt the operator to add the barrier product (brand + manufacturer) to the materials list and link the entry; give `PlanMaterialEntry` a label upload that ships in the packet (the C11 "11.1 (labels or photos attached)" fix). |
| 5.1-6 | I have listed all substances on my OSP Materials List section C11. (Yes.) | Partial | P1 | `materials_application.pest_disease_weed_listed` | Same verdict as CCOF Materials "B (listing evidence)": the attestation exists and prints, but the prefill still suggests 'Yes' from evidence of USE rather than of LISTING — a logged application makes the suggestion fire even when that product is not on the list. Suggest→confirm means the operator must accept it, so nothing is auto-answered, but the suggestion points the wrong way in exactly the case that matters. The module PDF now prints a [REVIEW] line naming logged products that match no plan entry (as UNMATCHED, never "unapproved" — a brand can be legitimately covered by a National List substance row), so the disagreement is at least stated beside the attestation rather than hidden. **Fix:** Resolve logged product names against the plan first; suggest nothing (and name the unmatched products in the suggestion basis) unless every logged product resolves; refuse an affirmative attestation while unmatched products remain, via the `attests_embed` gate G8.0 A1 already uses. |

One half of WSDA's gap does NOT apply here: OTCO asks the method question once, for the whole plan, so the single operation-wide answer is the right shape and only the axis is wrong. OTCO does not ask frequency or how results are recorded, so `monitoring_frequency` and `monitoring_records` are not cited (see otco/unmapped/g5_0_pest.yaml) — they exist, are required and print; this is a fact about OTCO's form. **Fix:** Add `monitoring_methods` [checkbox_group] {crop_health_observation, crop_yield_comparison, scouting, traps_lures, modeling, other} on page D beside `monitoring_scope` — the same fix WSDA F1 proposes; the per-pest-class split WSDA needs is optional for OTCO. |

OTCO adds five practices CCOF does not list — grasslands, standing deadwood, replacing weedy areas, allowing recolonisation, priority-species protection plans — none with an option. **Fix:** Same fix as CCOF A4 (add the four gated or missing options directly to `habitat_biodiversity_practices`) plus `standing_deadwood`, `grassland_woodland_restoration` and `priority_species_plan`. |

P2 rather than CCOF A6's P3 because three named practices, not only the catch-all, are unstateable. **Fix:** Same fix as CCOF A6 (`other` + free text) plus `grazing`, `biological_control` and `prescribed_burning`. |

### C9 Contamination Prevention

*C9 · rev. 2023/09/14 · retrieved 2026-09-09*

The form's own instruction: "Complete this form for both organic and non-organic production as indicated."

### Crop Producer Organic System Plan

*AGR 2121 · R 02/25 (sections A-R; §S is R 03/26) · retrieved 2026-08-28*  
<https://agr.wa.gov/departments/organic/forms-and-applications>

**When WSDA requires it:** Required of every operation applying for WSDA crop producer organic certification. WSDA runs a LIVING plan — it is completed once, and a renewing operation updates the sections that changed rather than re-filing it. The March 1 renewal deadline is the renewal application and fee.

**1 questions** — Partial 1

| Ref | What WSDA asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Header | Business Name; Cert No — printed in the running header of every page of this OSP form, beneath WSDA Organic Program's return address and Fee Code 4102. | Partial | P3 | `company.Company.name` · `certifications.Certification` | The cover prints the operation's legal name, certificate number and certifier. It does NOT print the certificate's effective date, expiry date or certified scope, which the `prints` line used to claim — `certificate_effective` is computed and never rendered (corrected 2026-08-28). **Fix:** Render effective date, expiry date and scope beside the certificate number on the cover. |

### D Soil Fertility and Crop Nutrient Management

*AGR 2121 · R 02/25 · retrieved 2026-08-28*  
<https://agr.wa.gov/departments/organic/forms-and-applications>

**When WSDA requires it:** Crop Producer Organic System Plan (AGR 2121) — filed once by every crop producer applicant; WSDA runs a LIVING plan, so a renewing operation updates the sections that changed rather than re-filing the whole OSP (the March 1 deadline is the renewal application and fee)

| 1 | How do you monitor soil health and soil organic matter? Crop quality / Crop yields / Microbiological testing / Observation of plant health / Observation of soil / Plant tissue testing / Soil testing / Other. | Partial | P1 | `g4_0_rotation_soil.fertility_monitoring` | WSDA asks this as one merged question, which is actually the shape Trazo's own `fertility_monitoring` list already has (CCOF's G4.0 splits the same content into a monitoring-methods B1 and a lab-testing-types B2, which Trazo's single list was registered against as `partial`/P1 for merging what CCOF keeps separate — that specific critique does not apply to WSDA's own, already-merged D1). What still does not line up is the option vocabulary: WSDA's 8 options include microbiological testing, crop-yield comparison and observation of soil, none of which exist in Trazo's 5-option list (`soil_tests, tissue_tests, organic_matter, crop_observation, no_testing`), and the exclusive `no_testing` option still blocks the common honest answer 'we observe but do not lab-test.' **Fix:** Add `microbiological_testing`, `crop_yield_comparison` and `soil_observation` to `fertility_monitoring`; drop the `no_testing` exclusive flag; add `daily`/`weekly` to `monitoring_frequency` (WSDA's 1a is open text, so any fixed radio will always be an approximation). |
| 1a | How often do you take these tests or make these observations? | Partial | P2 | `g4_0_rotation_soil.monitoring_frequency` | WSDA's 1a is open text; `monitoring_frequency` is a fixed radio without daily or weekly. **Fix:** Add `daily` and `weekly` to `monitoring_frequency`. |
| 2 | How do you manage soil health? (Animal manure / Annual crop rotation / Compost / Compost tea / Conservation cover - Perennial / Cover crop - Annual / Fallow rotations / Foliar fertilizers / Green manure / Incorporate crop or pruning residues / Mulching / Rock minerals / Soil inoculants / Other.) | Partial | P2 | `g4_0_rotation_soil.fertility_components` | Same underlying gap CCOF's G4.0 A2 already names for this field: `fertility_components` has no `other`, no foliar-fertilizer option, and one `compost` value where WSDA (like CCOF) separates compost from compost tea. WSDA's own list adds further absentees with no matching option at all: green manure, fallow rotations, conservation cover – perennial, and mulching (mulching exists in Trazo today only as a weed-control option on the pest module, not as a soil-fertility practice). **Fix:** Same fix as CCOF A2 — add `foliar_fertilizers`, `compost_tea`, `other` + free text. ### F Weed Management

*AGR 2121 · R 02/25 · retrieved 2026-08-28*  
<https://agr.wa.gov/departments/organic/forms-and-applications>

**When WSDA requires it:** Crop Producer Organic System Plan (AGR 2121) — filed once by every crop producer applicant; WSDA runs a LIVING plan, so a renewing operation updates the sections that changed rather than re-filing the whole OSP (the March 1 deadline is the renewal application and fee)

**9 questions** — Covered 2 · Partial 4 · Not covered 3

| Ref | What WSDA asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which monitoring practices do you implement to determine the effectiveness of your weed management plan? (Comparison of crop yields / Observation of crop health / Observation of weeds / Other.) | Partial | P1 | `g5_0_pest.monitoring_scope` | Right subject, wrong axis. `monitoring_scope` records WHAT is watched — pest populations, disease pressure, weed pressure, beneficial insect activity — so an operation that monitors weeds says so, and it prints. WSDA asks WHICH METHOD: comparison of crop yields, observation of crop health, observation of weeds, other. Only 'observation of weeds' falls in both, and it arrives here as a category rather than as a chosen technique, so a reviewer learns that weeds are monitored and not how. `monitoring_scope` is also single-valued across the whole operation, while WSDA asks the method question three times — once each for the weed (F1), pest (G1) and disease (H1) plans. **Fix:** Add a `monitoring_methods` [checkbox_group] {crop_yield_comparison, crop_health_observation, target_observation, trap_monitoring, modeling, scouting_program, other} on page D beside `monitoring_scope`, ideally per pest class so F1, G1 and H1 can each print their own answer. |
| 2 | How often do you make these comparisons or observations? | Partial | P2 | `g5_0_pest.monitoring_frequency` | The closest thing in the register to a clean answer: `monitoring_frequency` asks exactly this and offers at each field visit or scouting event / weekly / monthly / each season, and it prints. It is short of `covered` on one point only — it is ONE frequency for the whole operation, and WSDA asks the question separately for weed (F2), pest (G2) and disease (H2), so an operation scouting weeds weekly and modelling disease seasonally has to pick one and answer the other two wrongly. **Fix:** Make `monitoring_frequency` per pest class, alongside the F1 fix; a single generalised field cannot answer three separately-asked questions truthfully. |
| 3 | Which preventive weed control strategies do you implement on your operation? (Cover crop - Annual / Crop rotation / Crop spacing / Field preparation / Flame weeding / Hand weeding / Mechanical cultivation / Mowing / Natural mulch / Stale seed bed / Other.) | Partial | P1 | `g5_0_pest.weed_management_practices` · `g5_0_pest.weed_management_other` · `g5_0_pest.prevention_practices` · `g5_0_pest.prevention_practices_other` | CCOF asks these same practices inside ONE matrix (G5.0 §A, 23 practices × 4 pest-type columns: Weeds / Insects & invertebrates / Diseases & nematodes / Vertebrate pests), already registered `partial`/P1 there because Trazo's `prevention_practices` and `weed_management_practices` carry no pest-type dimension. WSDA makes the same underlying fact harder to answer cleanly, not easier: it splits pest management into three physically separate sections (this form, plus G Pest and H Disease), each expecting its own self-contained answer, instead of one table where a practice repeated across pest-type columns reads as normal. Half of WSDA's F3 list — crop rotation, crop spacing — lives in Trazo's generic, pest-type-blind `prevention_practices`, which a WSDA reviewer would see printed IDENTICALLY under the G and H sections too; in a matrix that reads as intentional (one row, several checked columns), across three independent PDF sections it reads as a copy-pasted answer that never differentiates weed-specific reasoning from disease-specific reasoning. The rest of the list (mechanical cultivation, hand weeding, mowing, natural mulch, flame weeding) does live in the weed-specific `weed_management_practices`, the right shape for this section — but even there, `crop_spacing`, `field_preparation` and `stale_seed_bed` have no matching option. On balance this does not rise to a bounced packet: the substantive content is present and responsive to the question asked. But it is more likely to draw an actual reviewer comment than CCOF's version of the same gap, because WSDA's layout puts the duplication in plain sight across three section headers instead of inside one table's columns, so this stays a P1 (request for information) rather than escalating. **Fix:** Same structural fix as CCOF's G5.0 §A: add a pest-type dimension to `prevention_practices` (matrix kind, or interim `pest_classes_addressed` checkbox group) so the compiled narrative can print a weed-specific paragraph for this section, a distinct one for G, and a distinct one for H instead of the same list three times. Also add `crop_spacing`, `field_preparation` and `stale_seed_bed` to `weed_management_practices`. |
| 4 | Do you use plastic mulch or silage tarps for weed control in an annual cropping system? Yes / No. | Partial | P2 | `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_used` | Use and season-end removal are captured. Missing is the § 205.601(b)(2)(ii)-(iii) non-PVC material condition CCOF's own G5.0 §A register row already flags as absent from these same two fields. **Fix:** Same fix already proposed on the CCOF side: add `plastic_mulch_non_pvc` [radio] {confirmed_non_pvc, biobased_film, unknown}, visible when `plastic_mulch_used`. |
| 4a | If yes, describe how you ensure it is removed from the field at the end of the growing or harvest season. | Covered | — | `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_removal` | — |
| 5 | Do you use plastic mulch or silage tarps for weed control in a perennial cropping system? Yes / No. | Covered | — | `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_used` | — |
| 5a | If yes, describe how you ensure the plastic remains in sufficient condition that prevents decomposition into the soil. | Not covered | P2 | — | `plastic_mulch_removal` is framed around season-end removal in an annual system ('describe how the plastic or synthetic mulch is removed at season end'); it does not ask WSDA's actual perennial-system question — how the operation ensures the plastic stays intact enough to avoid decomposing into the soil over a multi-year planting. A perennial-crop operator answering this field today is describing the wrong practice. **Fix:** Add `plastic_mulch_perennial_condition` [textarea], visible when the operation's cropping system includes `perennial` (per `g4_0_rotation_soil.system_type`), separate from the annual-system removal question. |
| 6 | Describe the records you maintain regarding your preventative weed management strategies. | Not covered | P2 | — | No field captures what records are kept for preventative weed-management practices specifically. `monitoring_records` (§ 205.201(a)(3)) is the nearest existing field and is NOT cited here, on the axis: it asks how MONITORING RESULTS are recorded, not what records document the preventative practices themselves. Those records exist in Trazo as logged events rather than as a described-records answer, which is a different artifact from the narrative WSDA asks for here. |---|---|---|---|---|---|

(Observation of crop health / Comparison of crop yields / Trap monitoring / Pest modeling / Scouting program / Other.) | Partial | P1 | `g5_0_pest.monitoring_scope` | Same shape as F1, and see that row for the correction history. `monitoring_scope` records that pest populations and beneficial-insect activity are watched, and it prints; WSDA asks which METHOD does the watching. WSDA additionally names 'trap monitoring' and 'pest modeling' as distinct techniques with no Trazo equivalent at all, so the method gap is wider here than under F. **Fix:** The F1 fix, with `trap_monitoring` and `modeling` among the options. |
| 2 | How often do you make these comparisons or observations? | Partial | P2 | `g5_0_pest.monitoring_frequency` | Same as F2: `monitoring_frequency` asks exactly this and prints, but it is one operation-wide answer against three separately-asked WSDA questions (F2 weed, G2 pest, H2 disease). **Fix:** Same fix as F2 — make `monitoring_frequency` per pest class. |
| 3 | Which crop pests do you manage? (Insects / Rodents / Birds / Nematodes / Mites / Slugs / Other.) | Not covered | P2 | — | No field asks which pest taxa the operation actually manages. CCOF's G5.0 matrix does not ask this either — it only offers generic 'Insects & invertebrates' and 'Vertebrate pests' columns, never enumerating species or taxa — so this is a genuinely fresh WSDA-specific ask with no CCOF row to reuse. Without it, `prevention_practices`'s vertebrate-specific options (`vertebrate_exclusion`, `raptor_habitat`, `vertebrate_trapping`) print with no stated target: rodents, birds, or both. **Fix:** Add `pest_taxa_managed` [checkbox_group] {insects, rodents, birds, nematodes, mites, slugs, other}. |
| 4 | Which preventative pest control strategies do you implement on your operation? (Crop rotation / Insect or rodent traps / Structures for wildlife / Beneficial habitat / Resistant varieties / Mating disruption / Timing of planting / Release of beneficials / Trap crops / Companion planting / Physical barriers / Physical removal / Other.) | Partial | P1 | `g5_0_pest.prevention_practices` · `g5_0_pest.prevention_practices_other` | Same three-way split named in full at F3: WSDA asks this as its own section rather than as extra columns on one matrix, so Trazo's pest-type-blind `prevention_practices` list prints the same generic text here as it does under F (weed) and H (disease) — a WSDA reviewer sees the identical paragraph three times with nothing that says which parts of it are actually about insects, rodents, birds, mites or slugs (the taxa ref 3 asks the grower to name). `Trap crops` and `companion planting` have no matching option in Trazo at all (CCOF's own G5.0 register already names `trap_crops` as `not_covered`); `mating disruption` and 'insect or rodent traps' are absent too — only `beneficial_habitat`, `beneficial_release`, `resistant_varieties`, and `vertebrate_trapping`/`vertebrate_exclusion` (a rough match for 'physical barriers' against vertebrates specifically, not insects or rodents generally) line up. As at F3, this is a request-for-information severity, not a bounce: the content that does exist is substantively responsive. **Fix:** Same structural fix as F3 — a pest-type dimension on `prevention_practices`. Additionally add `trap_crops` (per CCOF's own register), `companion_planting`, `mating_disruption` and `insect_rodent_traps` as options. |
| 5 | Describe the records you maintain regarding your preventative pest management efforts. | Not covered | P2 | — | Same gap as F6: no field captures what records document the preventative practices themselves, as distinct from monitoring-result records. `monitoring_records` is not cited here on that axis — see F6. **Fix:** Add `pest_prevention_records` [textarea]. |

| A1 | If crops are grown in buffer areas, how are they separated during harvest, storage, and sales? (Not applicable, no buffer crop grown / harvest containers are not marked 'organic' / crop is destroyed, given away, or not harvested / stored apart / harvested at different times / crops are not marked 'organic' on crop records / mark or flag buffer areas / sold to a different buyer than the organic / keep separate records to track harvest and sales / other.) 'Crop destroyed, given away, or not harvested' collapses into the single `do_not_harvest_buffer` option even though buffer-harvest event records (`buffer_disposition`) already distinguish not-harvested from disposed from given-away. The Parcel Application half of this row is CLOSED (2026-08-27): the parcel PDF used to derive a § 205.202(c) disposition — "never sold as organic" — from the free-text `crop_grown_in_buffer` field the operator uses only to name the crop. | A2 | What safeguards do you use to prevent contamination from drift? DriftWatch/registry name is not captured (`sensitive_crop_registry` has no name field). `roadside_utility_registration` is worded as a registration/request, not CCOF's written agreement. `self_managed_adjacent` is labeled 'no third-party spray risk' — a conclusion, not a fact, and one the compiled narrative prints verbatim — with no field to describe the actual precautions taken. 'Residue testing' (`residue_testing`) is worded as incident-driven, not CCOF's routine monitoring testing. `drift_response_procedure` is a Trazo-only superset question (§ 205.400(f)(1), answering the form's opening instruction to notify CCOF immediately of drift) rather than one of the ten checkboxes. **Fix:** Add an exclusive `none_no_surrounding_prohibited_use` option; add `drift_agreements_upload` [upload, opt] and wire `generate_osp_packet` to pull module uploads (tagged by `linked_section`) into `attachments/<module>/`, not just `receipts/`; add `drift_registry_name` [text]; split `roadside_utility_registration` into a registration option and a `roadside_agency_agreement` option (+ upload); relabel `self_managed_adjacent` and add a `self_managed_precautions` textarea; add `residue_testing_routine`. |

Whether that gate belongs on G6.0 (matching CCOF's own form) or stays on G4.2 is a design decision Trazo needs to make deliberately rather than by default; either way the two modules should agree on where irrigation lives. |

Surface the per-source badge (WSDA / OMRI / National List) in the operator-facing materials panel, not just the module PDF, and let the operator filter to 'not yet WSDA-listed' when preparing an Input Material List — so AGR 2196 only asks about what genuinely needs asking, and does not imply an OMRI-only match is already WSDA-cleared. |

The Materials List workbook already counts each blank per row (`fix_hint="materials_list"`) and the editor names where it is answered. ### OFPP Organic Fraud Prevention Plan

*OFPP · rev 2025/08/27 · retrieved 2026-09-09*  
<https://tilth.org/help-center/blank-forms-all/>

**When OTCO requires it:** C1 Crop Activities Checklist — "I/We are applying for Oregon Tilth organic certification for crop production" routes to "O1: Operation Information (required)" and "OFPP: Organic Fraud Prevention Plan". The form itself carries a not-applicable stop for perennial or wild-crop growers who buy no certified organic seed or planting stock (row 1-3).

**17 questions** — Covered 1 · Partial 12 · Not covered 4 · not questions: Instruction (asks nothing) 1

| Ref | What OTCO asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-1 | Section 1. ORGANIC FRAUD PREVENTION TEAM — identify the person or people responsible for approving, implementing, training staff, and monitoring the Organic Fraud Prevention Plan. Table: Name · Job Title/Role · Contact Info (Phone/Email). | Partial | P2 | `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_accuracy_process` · `company.Establishment.ofpp_responsible_person` | FRESH — neither CCOF G8.0 §D nor WSDA §P asks for a named team, so no verdict existed to reuse. Trazo holds ONE responsible name on the Establishment (`ofpp_responsible_person`: no title, no contact, dossier-only) and a prose answer in G2.0 §C that names who keeps the plan accurate. There is no table of name · role · contact, and the four responsibilities OTCO distinguishes — approve, implement, train, monitor — cannot be assigned to different people. **Fix:** Add a repeatable `ofpp_team` field {name, role, responsibilities (approve / implement / train / monitor), contact} to G2.0 page C, seeded from `ofpp_responsible_person` for the operator to confirm, printing as OTCO's table. |
| 1-2 | How will you report possible organic fraud? Check all that apply: report to your Oregon Tilth Client Services Team · report to the supplier's certifying agent · report to the USDA National Organic Program · report to the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) State Organic Program, for CA operations · other (describe). | Partial | P2 | `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_mitigation_practices` · `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_mitigation_other` | Reused from WSDA §P 6 (P2). `report_suspected` is one tick — "Report suspected fraud to our certifier or the NOP" — with no breakdown. WSDA wanted the TRIGGERS for a report; OTCO wants the CHANNELS (own certifier, the supplier's certifier, the NOP, CDFA). A certifier cannot tell from the tick whether a California operation knows CDFA is a reporting route, or whether the operation would report upstream to a supplier's agent. **Fix:** Add `fraud_reporting_channels` checkbox_group {own_certifier, suppliers_certifier, usda_nop, cdfa_sop, other} shown when `report_suspected` is selected — beside the `fraud_reporting_triggers` group WSDA §P 6 proposes. |
| 1-3 | If you grow perennial crops or harvest wild crops, do you buy certified organic products like seeds or planting stock? Yes / No — the Organic Fraud Prevention Plan is not applicable (stop here; you do not need to fill out the rest of the form) / N/A — I don't grow perennial crops or harvest wild crops. | Partial | P3 | `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_areas` | A DIVERGENCE, not a missing field. OTCO lets a perennial or wild-crop grower who buys no certified organic inputs declare the whole plan not applicable and stop. Trazo's G2.0 has `allows_not_applicable=False` on purpose — the federal Common OSP Section 2 offers no N/A, because SOE applies § 205.201(a)(3) to every certified operation — so the same grower answers all three pages, briefly (the `none` risk area, the mitigations they actually run, the review cadence). The packet therefore carries a full plan where OTCO would have accepted a stopped form, and nothing on the packet says this is deliberate, so a reviewer may read the extra pages as the operation misjudging its own scope. The three facts OTCO's gate turns on — perennial system (G4.0), wild crop (W2.0), certified inputs purchased (G3.0/G3.2) — are all in the plan but are never stated together. **Fix:** Do NOT add an N/A gate to G2.0. For an OTCO packet, state on 04-coverage-and-scope.pdf (or in the G2.0 module header) that the plan answers the fraud-prevention module in full under the federal template even where OTCO's OFPP would accept "not applicable", and print the three trigger facts beside it so the reviewer sees why the pages are short. |
| 1-4 | Does your operation already have an Organic Fraud Prevention Plan? No — complete this module / Yes — plan is attached; you can skip the rest of this module if your plan includes all the required sections, and complete any that are missing. | Partial | P2 | `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_plan_upload` · `company.Establishment.fraud_prevention_plan_document` · `company.Establishment.fraud_prevention_plan_date` · `company.Establishment.ofpp_on_file` | Reused from WSDA §P 1 (P2). An operation with a plan written elsewhere can attach it (`fraud_plan_upload`, or the farm profile's `fraud_prevention_plan_document`, which the readiness check accepts as "OFPP on file" alongside a completed G2.0), but no upload reaches `generate_osp_packet` — `osp_module_pdf` skips `kind in ("info", "upload")` and only parcel maps are written into the ZIP. OTCO's "Yes — attached" is therefore a statement the packet cannot back. **Fix:** Reuse §P 1 — carry module uploads into the packet ZIP the way `parcels/maps/` already travels, and print "plan attached: <filename>, dated <fraud_prevention_plan_date>" in G2.0's header when either upload exists. |

**When WSDA requires it:** "A renewal fee is due with your renewal application by March 1. This fee is based on the gross annual income received from organic crops, products, or services in the previous calendar year."

**6 questions** — Partial 4 · Out of scope 2

| Ref | What WSDA asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 1 | Gross annual income received in the last calendar year. | Partial | P2 | `history.SalesRecord.sale_amount` | 02 totals the sales invoiced as organic and dated in the prior calendar year, and says it is not reconciled and not AGR 2521's figure (run 3, R3-03). WSDA asks for income RECEIVED from organic crops, products or services, which counts payments, not invoices, and includes services. Fruit of the prior crop settled after 31 December is not in Trazo's subtotal, and 02 says so. **Fix:** Record payment dates on sales, total income received in the calendar year, and state any services income the operation enters. |

WSDA's question is about the application packet AND the fee payment, which may travel separately. **Fix:** Let the filing record the application and the payment methods apart. |

### C11 Crop Materials List

*C11 · rev. 2023/09/14 · retrieved 2026-09-09*  
<https://tilth.org/help-center/blank-forms-all/>

**When OTCO requires it:** C1 Crop Activities Checklist — "I/We utilize material inputs/products in our organic production system" → C11 Crop Materials. The form's own first checkbox ("Not Applicable; no materials/inputs are used") is how a grower with no inputs answers it, so in practice every grower files C11; it is also the form a certified operation files during the year to add a product to its current Materials List ("The products identified below are to be added to my current Materials List").

**9 questions** — Covered 1 · Partial 7 · Not covered 1

| Ref | What OTCO asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Instructions (all input materials) | Provide the names of ALL input materials and substances in use or intended for use in your Organic system. This Materials List must include all fertilizers, pest and disease control materials, compost and manure products, inoculants, planting mixes, seed treatments, cleaners and sanitizers, adjuvants, mulches, etc. | Partial | P2 | `materials_application.materials_list_panel` · `materials_application.materials_list_complete` · `materials_application.fertilizers_listed` · `materials_application.pest_disease_weed_listed` · `materials_application.production_aids_listed` · `materials_application.post_harvest_contact_listed` · `certifications.services.plan_materials (all FOUR sources — National List, OMRI, WSDA, operator-entered)` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.status` | Same verdict as WSDA AGR 2196 Hdr and CCOF NOPB41 Header B, brought up to date. OTCO asks for ONE list covering every category; Trazo holds one list, read through `plan_materials()` from all four sources, and attests completeness four times, once per category (fertilizers and soil amendments; pest, disease and weed control; production aids; post-harvest contact materials) — a more demanding shape than OTCO's single list, and a reviewer can see which class was left unattested. Since 2026-08-28 an operator-entered row (`PlanMaterialEntry`) can hold any of OTCO's named classes — compost, manure, planting mixes, mulches, inoculants — with a planned/in-use `status`, so "in use or intended for use" is stated for those rows and prints in the workbook's In use / Intended for use columns. Two gaps remain. (1) A material attached straight from a catalog (an OMRI, WSDA or National List FK with no operator row) carries no status, so the list states use for only part of itself. (2) Seed treatments logged on planting events and sanitizers logged on post-harvest events are never read into the rows (CCOF §C/§D carry this), so the operator has to retype them; the [REVIEW] reconciliation that names logged products missing from the plan reads chemical-application and soil-amendment events only. The siblings' gap text — "nothing records whether a row is planned, in use, or discontinued" — is now true only of catalog-attached rows. **Fix:** Require `status` on a catalog attach (create the operator row alongside the FK, as the fold in `plan_materials` already anticipates); read distinct `seed_treatment` and `sanitizer_name` values into `_material_rows` so the reconciliation and the workbook cover every class OTCO names; keep the four attestations. |
| 11.1 (not applicable) | Not Applicable; no materials/inputs are used. | Covered | — | `materials_application.no_materials_used` · `materials_application.fertilizers_none_used` · `materials_application.pest_disease_weed_none_used` · `materials_application.production_aids_none_used` · `materials_application.post_harvest_contact_none_used` · `materials_application.materials_list_complete` · `certifications.services.plan_materials.none_used_contradictions` | — |
| 11.1 (own list attached) | I have attached my own list with this information. | Partial | P2 | `materials_application.materials_list_panel` | Trazo's generated list IS the operator's own list, so this is the path an OTCO operation using Trazo takes — and OTCO's condition is that the attached list carry "this information", the four columns of the table. The two Trazo artifacts between them do not: the module PDF prints name — manufacturer — identifier grouped by source (no intended use); the workbook prints Product, Manufacturer, Reason for use, In use, Intended for use (no review agency). Neither prints the per-row OMRI / WSDA / OTHER position or a label reference. The column rows below state each shortfall; this row records that an OTCO reviewer receiving either artifact under this checkbox will find columns missing. **Fix:** Give the module PDF a four-column table matching C11 (name incl. formulation · manufacturer · review agency + identifier · intended use), built from the same `plan_materials()` rows the grouped list already uses, so the attachment carries every column the form asks for. |
| 11.1 (additions to current list) | The products identified below are to be added to my current Materials List. | Partial | P2 | `materials_application.materials_list_panel` · `certifications.models.ApprovedInputChangeLog (append-only; written by add_approved_input for catalog rows only)` · `certifications.models.OSPChangeNotification (category "Practice / input / procedure change — § 205.400(f)(2)")` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.created_at` | CCOF NOPB41 Header E ("to add or remove materials after your initial application, update your OSP Materials List") is `covered` on `ApprovedInputChangeLog` + `OSPChangeNotification`, and that verdict was right for the product it described: a material can be added to the list at any time, and a CATALOG attach writes a dated, append-only change-log row that the audit dossier prints and `plan_review` reads to flag `inputs_changed`. It is stale on one point since the operator-entered row shipped (2026-08-28): `ApprovedInputChangeLog` is written only by `add_approved_input` (kinds national_list / omri / wsda), so a `PlanMaterialEntry` added mid-year has a `created_at` and nothing else — no change-log row, nothing for `plan_review` to flag, and nothing in 03-change-notifications.pdf unless the operator files a § 205.400(f)(2) notification by hand. OTCO's checkbox exists precisely to separate "new since approval" from the standing list; Trazo cannot make that separation for operator-entered rows, which is the same "list what is NEW" gap WSDA AGR 2196 Hdr names. **Fix:** Write an `ApprovedInputChangeLog` row (or a parallel `PlanMaterialEntryChangeLog`) on every operator-entered create/delete; let the packet's materials page mark rows added since the plan was last submitted, and let a "C11 additions" view filter to them. |
| 11.1 (labels or photos attached) | Labels or photos of container are attached for each product that is not OMRI or WSDA listed. | Not covered | P1 | `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.listing_basis (identifies which rows have no OMRI or WSDA basis)` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.national_list_substance` | A fresh OTCO ask with no home in either sibling register. Trazo knows WHICH rows this applies to — every `PlanMaterialEntry` whose `listing_basis` is `national_list`, `certifier_letter` or `none_unlisted`, and every bare National List attach — but there is no per-material label or photo attachment anywhere: the row has no document field, DMS uploads are tagged by module rather than by material, and no module upload reaches the generated packet in any case. OTCO's rule also cuts across Trazo's claim ladder: a row whose basis is a National List SUBSTANCE prints "National List substance", which is a correct statement of its basis and is still, for OTCO, a product that is "not OMRI or WSDA listed" and needs its label — the statement can read as sufficient when for this form it is not. Nothing prompts the operator, so an OTCO reviewer receives the rows and no labels. **Fix:** Add a `label_document` upload on `PlanMaterialEntry`, prompted in the editor whenever `listing_basis` is not `omri` or `wsda` (including National List rows), shipped in the packet under `attachments/materials/<row>/` and named on the module page; print "label attached / label needed" beside each such row. |
| 11.1 Table (full product name) | Full Product Name, including any formulation (ex: "ABC Super Sulfur DF"). | Partial | P2 | `materials_application.materials_list_panel` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.product_name` · `certifications.services.plan_materials.PlanMaterial.display` | Closed 2026-09-09 (fix/parcel-page-land-history, materials cut): the certifier-facing line (`PlanMaterial.display(stated_absences=True)`, used by the module PDF and the plan snapshot) states a missing cell as missing — 'manufacturer not stated', 'reason for use not stated', and for a bare National List substance 'brand and formulation not stated' — instead of omitting it, so a row that needs the cell no longer reads like a row that never did. The Materials List workbook already counts each blank per row (`fix_hint="materials_list"`) and the editor names where it is answered. Remaining, as CCOF A (product name): no separate `formulation` field, and a National List attach does not yet require the operator row naming the brand applied. **Fix:** Same as CCOF A (product name). |

The Materials List workbook already counts each blank per row (`fix_hint="materials_list"`) and the editor names where it is answered. P1 → P2 because the row OTCO 'cannot review' now announces itself on the page and in the blank counter. Remaining: nothing requires the maker before submission (see CCOF A (manufacturer) for why not at create time). **Fix:** Completion gate on `manufacturer` for rows marked in use. |
| 11.1 Table (third party review agency) | Third Party Review Agency (ex: OMRI, WSDA) — per row, check OMRI / WSDA / OTHER. | Partial | P2 | `materials_application.materials_list_panel` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.listing_basis` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.certifier_letter_reference` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.omri_product` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.wsda_material` · `certifications.PlanMaterialEntry.national_list_substance` | A fresh OTCO column, adjacent to WSDA AGR 2196's "WSDA List cross-reference" row but a different ask (that row is about surfacing the per-source badge to the OPERATOR). For the OMRI and WSDA positions Trazo already prints the answer: each row sits under its source heading with the registry's own identifier, and the basis is checkable — `listing_basis` may say OMRI or WSDA only while the matching FK resolves, and the fold refuses to print a catalog number onto a row whose FK does not point at that exact listing. Trazo resolves the name; the operator's confirmed FK is the statement, and it is never OTCO's review. The OTHER position is the gap: everything else — a National List substance basis, a certifier's written approval, a row with no third-party listing — lands under OTHER on OTCO's form, and Trazo has no field to name the other reviewer. `certifier_letter_reference` is the nearest and covers only the letter case; there is nowhere to record that a manufacturer has supplied OTCO's Crop Input Verification Evaluation (a manufacturer-signed declaration, valid five years, which is what OTCO's OTHER column typically points at) or another ACA's review. The `listing_statement` for those rows — "National List substance", "no third-party listing on file" — is honest about the basis and says nothing about which agency, if any, reviewed the product. **Fix:** Add `other_review_agency` [text] and `other_review_reference` [text] on `PlanMaterialEntry`, visible when `listing_basis` is not `omri` or `wsda`; print the C11 trio per row (OMRI / WSDA / OTHER: <agency, reference>) in the module PDF table proposed at "11.1 (own list attached)". Never print a resolution as a review. |

Both exist only on operator-entered rows, and neither reaches the module PDF: `display()` prints name — manufacturer — identifier and nothing about use, so the list a reviewer reads has an empty Intended Use column on every row. The workbook prints the reason (or, for an event-derived row with no plan entry, the event type word — "Fertilizer", "Pest control"); a catalog-attached row with no operator entry and no logged application prints nothing anywhere. **Fix:** Print `category` (falling back to `reason_for_use`, then the event-type word) beside each row in the module PDF; require `category` on a catalog attach, the same way the "Instructions (all input materials)" fix requires `status`. |

| 7.10-4 | Attach a label for each product listed above and make sure to complete the C8 Labeling and Sales form. Attached. | Partial | P1 | `g7_0_labeling.label_files_upload` | The form asks for the label files here. Trazo collects them once, in `label_files_upload` on the labeling module; since 2026-10-01 they ride in the packet under labels/ (OSP alignment audit 2026-10, T19). This form is not yet named among the places they answer. **Fix:** Name this form among the places the uploaded label files answer. |
| 7.10-5 | How do you make sure the processing facilities you use are certified by a USDA-accredited certifier and stay in good standing? We keep valid certificates onsite that list the branded products and receive updated certificates every year / We check the Organic Integrity Database (OID) to confirm certificates are valid / Other (explain). | Partial | P1 | `g6_1_harvest_transport.uncertified_handler_records` · `g6_1_harvest_transport.off_farm_handler_table` · `certifications.PostHarvestFacility.cert_is_current` · `certifications.PostHarvestFacility.verification_status` · `certifications.PostHarvestFacility.last_verified_at` · `certifications.PostHarvestFacility.verification_source` | Reuses WSDA §L 1a (partial P1, same root cause) and 1b (not covered). Trazo holds the facts behind both of OTCO's options — a certificate on file with effective and expiry dates, and a check of the handler's certificate against the USDA Organic Integrity Database recorded as `verification_status` / `last_verified_at` — and prints the certificate line, but never asks or prints the operation's stated METHOD or its cadence ("updated certificates every year"), and the OID check result itself stays off the plan. The check is Trazo comparing a record to a public database; the packet must say "checked against", never "verified by". **Fix:** Print the OID check (source and date) on the facility line, and add `handler_cert_verification_method` [checkbox_group] {certificates_on_file_annual, oid_check, other} plus the WSDA 1b cadence radio to the G6.1 §D block. |

Consequence: choosing purchased vermicompost or compost tea (bought, not produced — bagged worm castings are common) opens `compost_method`, `compost_initial_cn_ratio`, `compost_temp_and_days` and `compost_temp_logs_kept` as REQUIRED questions, so the operator must type a thermophilic-process answer for a product they never produced. **Fix:** Add a second checkbox_group `materials_produced` {compost, compost_tea, vermicompost, none (exclusive)}, visible when `materials_applied` is not none; gate page C on `materials_produced` instead of `materials_applied`. |
| A2a | List all feedstocks/ingredients in the compost, vermicompost and/or compost tea you produce. If you produce more than one, provide separate ingredient lists for each. | Not covered | P1 | — | No feedstock question exists. The pilot packet shows the workaround in practice: the farm typed its feedstocks ('carrot and onion wash-line trim and spoiled straw against flail-chopped prunings…') into the C:N-ratio answer instead, because that was the only free-text field available. **Fix:** Add textarea `compost_feedstocks`, required when `materials_produced` is truthy, with coaching for one list per product; prefill from the `SoilManagementEvent.compost_feedstock` field already logged on composting events. |
| A2b | If you produce compost containing manure (and/or compost tea made from it), which production method do you use? Not applicable / windrow — reaches 131-170°F for at least 15 days, turned at least 5 times / in-vessel or static aerated pile — reaches 131-170°F for at least 3 days (maintain compost production records) / my compost does not meet either requirement, so it is considered 'raw manure' (complete section B). | Partial | P1 | `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_method` · `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_initial_cn_ratio` · `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_temp_and_days` · `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_turnings` · `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_temp_logs_kept` | Superset on the numbers actually asked (C:N ratio, temperature range, turning count, kept logs) for the two real thermophilic pathways. Three defects: `compost_method` lists `vermicompost` as one of its own options, a category error (vermicompost is CCOF's separate A2c question, not a thermophilic method) that forces the required temperature/day/turning questions onto a worm system never meant to answer them; there is no selectable 'does not meet either requirement, so it is raw manure' outcome that opens page B; and there is no N/A for compost containing no manure at all, so plant-only compost (unrestricted under § 205.203(c)(3)) is still forced through the required thermophilic questions. **Fix:** Remove `vermicompost` from `compost_method` and from the temperature/turning fields' `visible_when`; add a `compost_contains_manure` boolean gate; replace the implicit failure case with an explicit `does_not_meet` option that reveals page B. |
| A2c | If you produce vermicompost containing manure, are the following conditions met: aerobic conditions and 70-90% moisture maintained during production; composting duration sufficient to produce a finished product that does not contribute to contamination by plant nutrients, pathogens, heavy metals or prohibited-substance residues? Not applicable / Yes, maintain vermicompost production records and any test results / my vermicompost does not meet these requirements, so it is considered 'raw manure' (complete section B). | Partial | P2 | `g4_1_compost_manure.vermicompost_moisture` | Trazo asks one optional free-text moisture field where CCOF wants two attestations (aerobic conditions, sufficient duration), a records-kept confirmation, and a 'does not meet → raw manure' outcome. **Fix:** Add radio `vermicompost_conditions_met` {yes_records_kept, does_not_meet_raw_manure}, visible when `materials_produced` includes vermicompost; keep the moisture text as optional supporting detail. |
| B1 | Do you apply raw animal manure (including any compost, compost tea, or vermicompost containing manure that does not meet the section A production requirements), and/or do you have planned grazing of animals in your organic crop production areas? No (stop, form complete) / Yes, raw animal manure is applied / Yes, my operation uses planned grazing of animals in organic crop production areas. | Partial | P1 | `g4_1_compost_manure.materials_applied` | Page B's gate is `materials_applied includes raw_manure` only — there is no planned-grazing trigger at all, although the model already has `GR` (grazing) events with animal type/count/duration/purpose, the packet already computes a § 205.203(c)(1) grazing interval from them, and G5.0's weed-management question already offers 'Livestock grazing' as an option. A sheep-grazed orchard — routine in WA/CA orchards and vineyards — tells G5.0 it grazes and tells G4.1 'none of these are used', so the compiled § 205.201(a) narrative states something false by omission. **Fix:** Add `Option("planned_grazing", …)` to `materials_applied` (or a standalone boolean) and widen page B's `visible_when` to `includes_any (raw_manure, planned_grazing)`; relabel the `none` option; prefill a suggestion from `GR` events. |
| B2 | How do you meet the following restriction on the use of raw manure, either applied or from planned grazing? Mark all that apply. Used for crops that are not for human consumption / incorporated at least 120 days before harvest of crops whose edible portions contact soil or soil particles / incorporated at least 90 days before harvest of crops whose edible portions do not contact soil or soil particles. | Partial | P1 | `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_interval_rule` · `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_timing_detail` | CCOF says 'mark all that apply'; Trazo's `raw_manure_interval_rule` is a single-select radio, so a diversified farm with both root crops and tree or bush crops cannot state both rules truthfully. Separately, the packet's own crop classifier that decides which sub-cite to print (§ 205.203(c)(1)(i) vs (ii)) treats any crop as soil-contact by default and its keyword override list omits blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, kiwi and hops — so an operator who correctly answers 'no soil contact, 90 days' for blueberries still gets the packet printing the 120-day soil-contact citation and can be flagged for a classification mismatch despite answering correctly. **Fix:** Change `raw_manure_interval_rule` to a `checkbox_group`. Separately (outside this module), extend `_manure_interval_rule_for_crop`'s keyword list or set `has_soil_contact=False` for the elevated berry/cane/kiwi/hop crops in the seeder. |
| B3 | How do you ensure that manure does not contaminate wells, rivers or streams, lakes or ponds? | Partial | P1 | `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_water_risk` | CCOF requires an answer here; Trazo's `raw_manure_water_risk` is `required=False`, so a complete module can leave it blank. It is also only reachable when `materials_applied` includes raw_manure, so it never appears for the planned-grazing case even though § 205.203(c) applies to both. **Fix:** Set `required=True`; widen `visible_when` to `includes_any (raw_manure, planned_grazing)` once the B1 grazing trigger exists; cite § 205.203(c) explicitly. |

And the two modules can disagree, because nothing reconciles a 'no' on `storage_pest_control_materials_used` against a G9.0 answer describing bait stations. **Fix:** Add an exclusive `no_pest_control_materials_used` option to contamination_prevention. |

Not applicable, my business does not plan to use a synthetic input in organic handling or storage areas. | Not covered | P2 | `g9_0_facility_pest.material_tier` · `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation` | material_tier=synthetic_approved implies certifier pre-approval exists, and preventive_measures_documentation (visible for both national_list and synthetic_approved tiers) records how prevention was shown insufficient before ANY material is applied — but neither asks the specific, narrower justification WSDA wants: why National List materials specifically were determined ineffective before escalating to a non-listed synthetic.
