### Site Update Information

*AGR 2516 · R 01/20 · retrieved 2026-08-28*  
<https://agr.wa.gov/departments/organic/forms-and-applications>

**When WSDA requires it:** File when the Crop Production Information on your Certified Operation Profile no longer matches your plan for the coming year — crop, variety or acreage changes, or reduced total site acreage.

**3 questions** — Partial 1 · Not covered 2

| Ref | What WSDA asks | Status | Sev | Where it lives in Trazo | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Instructions (changes per site) | Indicate what changes need to be made for each site where the Crop Production Information on the Certified Operation Profile does not match your current plan for the coming year — crops/varieties, acreages, and whether total site acreage will be reduced. Alternatively, production or planting records may be submitted instead, provided they clearly indicate the site number and site name as identified on your certificate. | Partial | P1 | `certifications.models.OSPChangeNotification` · `certifications.models.OSPAnnualUpdate` | The packet already carries a superset mechanism — `OSPChangeNotification` (categories include `acreage_field_addition` and `field_removal`, both citing § 205.400(f)(2)) and `OSPAnnualUpdate`'s `additions`/`deletions` JSON — so the SUBSTANCE of a site update is capturable. But neither is structured by a WSDA-assigned SITE NUMBER, which is the specific cross-reference WSDA's own Certified Operation Profile needs to locate the record; `OSPChangeNotification.parcel` links to Trazo's own `Parcel` row, and the parcel module has no `wsda_site_number` field at all (same gap as AGR 2264 ref '6'). **Fix:** Add the `wsda_site_number` field proposed for AGR 2264 ref '6' to the parcel module, and print it beside the parcel name on any WSDA-bound change notification or annual-update page. |
| Table (site, name, changes) | Table: WSDA site no., WSDA site name, and a plain-language description of the change (e.g., 'total site acreage remains the same', '5 acres moved to conventional, organic acreage is now 15 acres'). | Not covered | P2 | `certifications.models.OSPChangeNotification.description` | `OSPChangeNotification.description` is free text and can hold the same plain-language change statement WSDA's own table wants, but without the `wsda_site_number` field (see 'Hdr'), the printed change-notification page cannot reproduce WSDA's own two leftmost columns — a reviewer matching this page against the Certified Operation Profile has to do it by parcel name alone. **Fix:** Same as 'Hdr': add `wsda_site_number`, and format the printed row as 'WSDA site no. / site name / description' when it is set. Once captured, Trazo's own production and crop-history records could also double as the 'alternative records' AGR 2516 says may be submitted instead of this form — they cannot today, for the same reason. |
| Instructions (acreage removed) | If acreage is removed from organic production, include a map identifying the new boundaries and include details on why the acreage was removed (e.g., transferred to another grower, converted to conventional). | Not covered | P1 | — | AGR 2516 asks for a boundary map AND the reason acreage was removed — and only when acreage is removed, with the form itself accepting "production records, planting records, etc." in place of the map. Re-registered on 2026-08-28: the map half is conditional and substitutable, so it is not the map defect. The other half is an unconditional Trazo defect of its own — `OSPChangeNotification.supporting_document` is a real writable FileField with NO UI writer (the panel says so itself), it is never written into the packet ZIP, and `_change_notifications_pdf` never names it. There is no `removal_reason` field either: `description` carries an ADDITION example in both help text and placeholder. So landing the shared map service would close the map half and still leave a WSDA reviewer reading "5 acres moved to conventional" with no reason and nothing attached. **Fix:** Two moves, both independent of the map service: (1) give `OSPChangeNotification` an upload control and write `supporting_document` into the packet ZIP alongside `receipts/`, naming it in `_change_notifications_pdf`; (2) add a `removal_reason` prompt shown when the change reduces certified acreage, and stop illustrating `description` with an addition. |

## Forms Trazo does not register

CCOF's Guide routes by activity, so what is absent is as readable as what is present.
A **decision** is an answer; a **gap** is a debt, and names where it is triggered from.

### Gaps

| Form | Triggered from | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Co-Packer Application (NOPB26) | G7.0 C — packing into a brand owned by another company | Trazo does not generate this form. An operation that packs its crop into a brand owned by another company files the Co-Packer Application with CCOF directly. |
| Exempt Handler Affidavit (NOPB107) | G6.1 A2/A3 (uncertified harvester or transporter); G6.2 A (uncertified storage); G6.5 A1 (uncertified supplier) | Trazo does not generate this form. Where an uncertified harvester, transporter, storage site or supplier handles this operation's crop, the affidavit is filed with CCOF directly. |
| IS – Independent & Off-Site Storage (IS) | C1 routing (stores crops at a non-certified facility that does not open, re-label or process the product, one per facility) and the C7 §7.7 storage table documentation column IS | Trazo does not generate this sheet. It is answered and signed by the manager of the uncertified warehouse or storage facility, and a copy is kept by both parties. Where this operation stores crop it still owns at such a facility, the plan records the facility by name and location in its storage section; the facility's own sheet is filed with the agent directly. |
| Private Label Agreement (PLA) (Private Label Agreement) | C8 §8.3 — packing organic crop into another company's brand or label when that brand owner is not itself certified | Trazo does not generate this agreement. The plan records, in its labeling section, that crop leaves the operation under a buyer's label and the label claim the operation makes; the brand owner's certificate, or the agreement between the operation and an uncertified brand owner, is collected by the operation and filed with the agent directly. |
| Additional Facilities and Third-Parties (AGR 2519) | AGR 2121 §B 2 (off-site seedling production); §J 13, §K 1, §L 1 (third-party handling, storage and post-harvest); §O 5 (records held off site) | Trazo does not generate this form. Where another operation handles, stores or post-harvest processes this crop, the plan records that operation by name, address, role and certificate status, and prints it in the harvest, storage and post-harvest sections — but the agent's own facilities form is filed directly. |
| Organic Label Approval Verification (AGR 2724) | AGR 2121 §N (labeling) — any label bearing an organic claim or the agent's mark | Trazo does not generate this form, and label artwork is not attached to this plan. The labeling section records how product is identified and what claims are used; the artwork itself goes to the agent directly for approval. |

### Deliberately not built

| Form | Reason |
|---|---|
| W2.0 Wild Crop Harvesting (NOPB48) | Trazo ships an N/A-attestable stub module so a crop grower can record that wild-crop harvesting does not apply, which is what a crop-scope OSP needs. An operation that does harvest wild crop files the full W2.0 with CCOF directly: its designated-area, 36-month harvest-site history and harvest-sustainability content is outside this plan's scope of cultivated orchard and berry ground. |
| Handler / Processor OSP forms (H-series) (NOPB32) | Trazo covers simple on-farm post-harvest handling of a farm's own crop (CCOF G6.4). Complex handling, multi-ingredient products and third-party processing are a different certification scope and a different product. A farm needing the H-series files it with its certifier directly. |
| Livestock OSP forms (L-series) (Guide to Livestock Producer OSP Forms) | Crop scope only. Nothing in the data model represents animals, feed, origin of livestock or living conditions, and pretending otherwise on a form would be worse than the absence. |
| Retail Establishment forms (R-series) (R1.0–R5.0) | Retail and restaurant operations are not producers. Out of scope by definition. |
| OCal Cultivator and Handler forms (OCal C-series / OCal H-series) | OCal is California's comparable-to-organic standard for cannabis. Different crop, different statute, different market. |
| COR (Canada) Handler forms (COR H-series) | Canadian Organic Regime equivalence. Out of scope while the market is US crop producers. |
| Global Market Access Application; Mexico Compliance Program; NOP Import Certificate Request (GMA04) | Export-programme enrolment and the certificates themselves are transactions between the operation and CCOF. Trazo captures the export and import questions the Common OSP asks (destination countries, certificate types, request-and-retain process, port integrity) inside G8.0 page C, which is the recordkeeping half — it does not file for the certificates. |
| Contracted Partner Program Application (Guide item 17) | An arrangement where a CCOF-certified customer manages the grower's certification. A grower in that programme has no OSP of their own to keep. |
| Certification Transfer Form (Certification Transfer Form) | Filed by an operation moving between certifying agents, which is a one-time transfer arrangement between the operation and the two agents rather than a fact about how the operation is farmed. An operation transferring certification files it directly. |
| T&C – Terms and Conditions (T&C) | The certification services and trademark-use terms (rev. 2023/09/14) that bind the operation to its certifying agent. They carry no signature block of their own: they are incorporated by reference and accepted by signing the Operation Information affirmations or the OSP Update Application and Agreement. Nothing is drafted from the operation's records. |
| C1 – Crop Activities Checklist (C1) | The checklist that routes an operation to the plan sections its activities require. The packet's coverage page performs that routing for this operation in the agent's own form numbers, so the checklist is not reproduced as a separate document; the operation ticks it directly when the agent asks for it. |
| A1 – Aquaponics, Container, and Greenhouse Production (A1) | Applies to crops grown in containers or aquaponics, to seedlings or transplants grown indoors for sale, to indoor structures that are not on certified land, and to greenhouses shared by organic and non-organic production. Crops grown in the ground under a high tunnel or hoop house do not need it. This plan does not describe those systems, so an operation that has any of them completes A1 with the agent directly. |
| C13 – Producer Group Operation (C13) | Applies to a grower cooperative certified as one multi-site operation under an internal control system (7 CFR 205.201(c)). This plan describes a single operation; a producer group files C13 with the agent directly. |
| C14 – Incubator Operation (C14) | Applies to an incubator operation that assists start-up farms with access to land. This plan describes a single operation managing its own parcels; an incubator files C14 with the agent directly. |
| W1 – Wild Crop Harvest (W1) | Trazo ships an N/A-attestable stub module so a crop grower can record that wild-crop harvesting does not apply, which is what a crop-scope plan needs. An operation that does harvest wild crop files the full W1 with the agent directly: its designated-area, harvest-site history and harvest-sustainability content is outside this plan's scope of cultivated orchard and berry ground. |
| Commercial Availability Form (CAF) (CAF) | A worksheet documenting one commercial-availability search, one form for each non-organic agricultural product or ingredient. It is written mainly for handlers; a farm may use it to document the search for non-organic seed, which has to be made each time non-organic seed is planted. The plan records whether a search precedes the use of non-organic seed and which search records the operation keeps; the worksheets themselves are the operation's own records, kept for inspection rather than generated by the plan. |
| Contact Change Form (Contact Change Form) | Notifies the agent of a change to the operation's contacts and their permissions. It is an administrative update to the agent's client record and is filed by the operation directly. |
| Crop Input Verification Evaluation (Manufacturer Declaration for Crop Inputs) (Crop Input Verification Evaluation) | A declaration the MANUFACTURER or its legal designee completes and signs about one input material — ingredients, extraction methods, excluded-methods status — valid for five years. The operation requests it from the manufacturer for any material that is not listed by a third-party review agency and keeps it with its input records; the operation cannot author a manufacturer's own attestation. |
| Land Transfer Form (Land Transfer Form) | Transfers a parcel between two operations both certified by this agent, when the field was inspected within the last twelve months, so that the parcel is added without a new inspection. It is signed by both the releasing and the receiving operation and filed with the agent directly; the receiving operation's plan records the parcel once it is on its certificate. |
| Manure Verification (Manure Verification) | A statement the manure SUPPLIER completes about the source and treatment of purchased manure. The plan records whether raw manure is applied, the pre-harvest interval it is held to and how water contamination is prevented, in its soil fertility section; the supplier's own statement is collected by the operation and kept with its input records. |
| Wood and Livestock Bedding Verification (Wood and Livestock Bedding Verification) | A statement the SUPPLIER of wood products or livestock bedding completes about treatments and additives. The plan lists such materials on the operation's materials list; the supplier's own statement is collected by the operation and kept with its input records. |
| OTCO Fee Schedule 2026 (OTCO Fee Schedule 2026) | The agent's published fee schedule, used with the renewal application to compute the certification fee from reported gross organic sales. It is the agent's own document, not a form the operation completes. |
| Handler Organic System Plan (AGR 2180) | Trazo covers simple on-farm post-harvest handling of a farm's own crop (WSDA Crop Producer OSP §K Storage, §L Post-Harvest). Complex handling, multi-ingredient products and third-party processing are a different certification scope and a different product — WSDA certifies handling under a separate Handler OSP (product flow, equipment cleaning and sanitation). A farm needing the Handler OSP files it with WSDA Organic Program directly. |
| Processed Product Application (AGR 2523) | Application to add a processed (multi-ingredient) product to a handler's certified scope. Same handler/processor certification scope excluded above — Trazo does not carry a farm into a handler-scope application. |
| Handled Product Application (AGR 2524) | Application to add a handled (single-ingredient, minimally processed) product to a handler's certified scope. Same handler/processor certification scope exclusion as AGR 2523. |
| Multi- and Single-Ingredient Processed Product Formulation (AGR 2178 / AGR 2179) | Ingredient-percentage formulation worksheets for a handler's processed-product recipe. Handler-side; a grower shipping raw or lightly-handled crop has no 'formulation' to declare. Same handler/processor scope exclusion. |
| Natural Flavor Questionnaire (AGR 2700) | Characterizes a purchased natural-flavor ingredient's own processing, for a handler's product formulation. Handler-side ingredient sourcing; same scope exclusion. |
| Non-Organic Ingredient Affidavit (AGR 2252) | Attests to a nonorganic ingredient used in a handler's multi-ingredient product. Handler-side product formulation, not something a crop grower selling raw or lightly-handled produce needs. |
| Ingredient Commercial Availability (AGR 2251) | WSDA's handler-side commercial-availability worksheet for a nonorganic ingredient in a processed product. Handler scope; same exclusion. It is not the grower-side seed and planting-stock commercial-availability search, which this plan does answer. |
| New Application for Organic Certification (AGR 2500) | The one-time application an operation files to enter the organic program — contacts, sites, products and the signed agreement. Trazo serves already-certified operations preparing an annual renewal, so the plan starts from an existing certification rather than establishing one. A first-time applicant files this directly. |
| Annual Renewal Application (Renewal application) | The renewal application a certified operation files with WSDA by March 1 each year ("your business must renew your application by March 1 each year"). WSDA does not publish it among its blank forms, so it is not reproduced here. The year's changes it asks for are on the annual update pages of this packet, and the site update (AGR 2516) and renewal fee (AGR 2521) forms are listed with it. |
| Organic Contact Information (AGR 2515) | Names and contact details for the people the agent corresponds with. The plan records the operation's responsible person and prints it on the packet cover; keeping the agent's own contact roster current is done with the agent directly. |
| New Applicant Fee (AGR 2499) | A fee paid by the operation to the agent. It sets what certification costs, not how the operation farms. |

## What Trazo asks that the registered forms do not

Not gaps — questions the federal Common OSP or the regulation itself asks for, which a
certifier's own grower overlay leaves implicit. Stated per agent: a question one asks and
the other does not is the most informative row here.

### CCOF

| Question | Why it has no CCOF counterpart |
|---|---|
| `certification_contract.contract_scopes` | Maps to the Contract's cover-page guide selection ('Guide to Grower OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Handler OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Livestock Producer OSP Forms' / 'Guide to Retail Establishment OSP Forms') rather than to any of the Contract's own lettered/numbered questions (A-H); Trazo captures the choice as a structured field instead of a forms checklist. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_mitigation_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `fraud_mitigation_practices`; not a separate CCOF question. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_plan_upload` | Optional upload for a written fraud-prevention plan. CCOF's G8.0 D references an external 'Fraud Prevention Plan worksheet' as guidance and reserves the right to request one for complex operations, but the grower form itself does not ask for an attachment. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `fraud_risk_areas`; not a separate CCOF question — G8.0 D1 is a fixed checklist of scenarios with no open-ended 'other'. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_accuracy_process` | Who keeps the OSP accurate, and how. The Certification Contract B2 asks only review FREQUENCY (annually/quarterly/monthly/other); it does not ask who performs the review or how, which this question captures beyond what either form requests. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_implementation_monitoring_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `osp_implementation_monitoring`; not a separate CCOF question. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.product_testing_detail` | Free-text elaboration (what is tested, and how often) for the `product_testing` option inside `fraud_mitigation_practices`; not asked as its own CCOF question. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.planting_stock_description` | CCOF's G3.0 has no general planting narrative question. This is the § 205.103 source-and- planting record (where the stock came from, where and when it was planted) Trazo captures for the invoice-to-block trace an inspector performs — beyond anything G3.0 itself asks. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.planting_stock_upload` | The attachment mechanism for `stock_records_kept` above; same reason — CCOF's G3.0 has no numbered question calling for a stock-paperwork upload. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_records_kept` | CCOF's B3 asks for commercial-availability search records specifically. This is Trazo's broader general recordkeeping battery for the stock itself (invoices, organic certificates, variety tags, phytosanitary certificates, planting map, treatment statements) — CCOF has no distinct numbered question for it beyond the generic inspection-records expectation in G8.0. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_treatments` | CCOF's G3.0 section D asks about SEED treatments only; it has no question about whether purchased planting stock itself was treated before or at delivery. Trazo superset for § 205.204 traceability. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_types_established` | CCOF's G3.0 asks only whether planting stock is organic or non-organic (A3); it never asks which propagation forms (bare-root, containerized, rootstock, cuttings/scions, crowns/divisions) were established. Trazo's own § 205.103 establishment-record granularity. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.suppliers_on_supplier_list` | CCOF's G3.0 never asks whether stock suppliers are entered on a Supplier List — that traceability expectation lives in Common OSP § 11 / G8.0 Record Keeping, not on the G3.0 form itself. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_documentation` | CCOF's G4.1 requires only that purchased compost/manure appear on the Grower Materials Application (OSP Materials List, section A1); it does not ask the operator to keep the supplier's process description or analysis on file. Trazo superset. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_upload` | The attachment mechanism for `purchased_compost_documentation` above; same reason. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_source` | Asked by OTCO C4 §4.3 (is the manure purchased or produced off-farm). This certifier's G4.1 asks whether raw manure is applied and how the interval and water-protection rules are met, never where the manure comes from. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_supplier_statement` | Asked by OTCO C4 §4.3 (label or supplier statement that purchased manure is untreated). This certifier's forms ask for no manure-provenance document; the material's listing is judged on the Materials Application instead. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.water_quality_test_frequency` | Companion frequency field to `water_quality_tested` above; same reason. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.water_quality_tested` | Trazo's own addition — feeds the `natural_resources_condition` record type — with no counterpart on either NOPB43 or NOPB40's section D. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_frequency` | § 205.201(a)(3) monitoring plan. CCOF's G5.0 (NOPB42) has no monitoring section — this is superset tracking of how often pest/disease/weed monitoring is performed, with suggestions derived from the median gap between logged scouting records. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_records` | § 205.201(a)(3) monitoring plan. CCOF's G5.0 (NOPB42) has no monitoring section — this is superset tracking of how monitoring results are recorded. |

CCOF's G5.0 (NOPB42) has no monitoring section — this is superset tracking of what is monitored (pest populations, disease pressure, weed pressure, beneficial activity), paired with monitoring_frequency and monitoring_records below. |
| `g6_0_production.nonorganic_system_materials` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.4 (a list of materials used in the non-organic production system). | `g6_0_production.runoff_mitigation_plan` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.3 (the runoff mitigation plan). Follows the runoff-risk question above, which this certifier does not ask. |
| `g6_0_production.runoff_risk_present` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.3 (risk of runoff carrying prohibited materials onto organic land). This certifier asks about drift and about buffers per border; water-borne contamination from neighbouring land is not a separate question. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.containers_reused_barrier` | Companion detail field to containers_reused_from_prohibited — same reasoning. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.containers_reused_from_prohibited` | §205.272(b)(2) prohibits reusing a container/bin/trailer that held a prohibited substance for organic product unless adequately cleaned. No CCOF grower form among G6.1/G6.2/G6.4/G6.5 asks this as its own distinct numbered question — it is folded into the general "packaging materials... free of prohibited substances" concept (G6.4 C, answered on G6.1 §B per that row's cross-citation). Trazo asks container reuse from a prior prohibited-substance contact as its own explicit gate. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.lot_identification_on_every_load` | §205.103(b)(2) traceability fact. CCOF's G6.1 form does not carry a distinct numbered checkbox for lot identification on every load — it is implied by the form's general instruction that "records must be sufficient to trace organic crops/products from production to sale or transport." Trazo tracks it as its own boolean, tying lot identity through transport as FSMA 204 KDE preparation (see also g6_2_storage.lot_identity_maintained). |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.transport_units_inspected_clean` | §205.272(a) contamination-prevention fact. CCOF's G6.1 form addresses this only as general framing text ("you must use management practices and physical barriers to prevent commingling... and to prevent contamination from contact with prohibited substances") and via the B1 equipment-cleaning table, not as a distinct numbered checkbox for transport units specifically. Trazo asks it as its own explicit gate under "C. Transport & lot identity." |
| `g6_2_storage.lot_identity_maintained` | §205.272 / §205.103(b)(2) traceability fact. CCOF's G6.2 form does not ask a distinct "does every stored lot keep its lot identity" checkbox anywhere in Sections A or B. Trazo asks it as its own boolean, tying lot identity through storage as FSMA 204 KDE preparation (see also g6_1_harvest_transport.lot_identification_on_every_load). |
| `g6_4_handling.commingling_controls` | §205.272(a) commingling-prevention fact. CCOF's G6.4 form is scoped to all-organic, single-operation handling where commingling with nonorganic product is defined out of scope by the form's own applicability gate ("this form does not apply if you are handling both organic and nonorganic products"). Trazo still asks it to cover the custom_handling_separation branch (handling another grower's product), where a commingling risk exists even within an all-organic-status framing. |
| `g6_4_handling.commingling_controls_other` | Companion detail field to commingling_controls — same reasoning. |
| `g6_4_handling.handling_records` | §205.103(b) recordkeeping fact. CCOF's G6.4 form does not itemize a records checklist — general recordkeeping obligations are covered by the separate G8.0 Record Keeping form. Trazo asks a handling-specific records checklist here as a superset. |
| `g6_4_handling.post_harvest_water_source` | Municipal / on-site well / other — WSDA §L 13 and OTCO C7 7.5-2. CCOF's G6.4 asks about what is ADDED to the water (B2), never where it comes from; the in-field form G6.1 B3 asks whether on-site treated water meets the Safe Drinking Water Act standard, which is a different fact and is registered there. |
| `g6_4_handling.post_harvest_water_uses` | What the post-harvest water is used for (equipment cleaning, crop washing, cooling, product transport, other) — WSDA AGR 2121 §L 12's checklist. CCOF's G6.4 B2 asks only whether water contacts organic product and what is added to it; the use does not change what B2 asks next. |
| `g7_0_labeling.organic_label_categories` | § 205.301 labeling-category tier (100% organic / organic / made with organic). CCOF's G7.0 does not ask which tier an operation sells under as its own question — it only asks about container types, seals, and statements — so this is Trazo capturing an implicit § 205.301 fact the grower form does not itself request. |
| `g7_0_labeling.product_leaves_as_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `product_leaves_as`; not a separate CCOF question — G7.0 A/B ask yes/no per container type, not an open-ended 'other' category. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.additional_records_locations` | Follow-up to `records_location`; see that entry. CCOF has no counterpart question. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.export_certificate_process` | Superset — how export certificates are requested, verified, and kept. CCOF's G8.0 A1 table only lists 'NOP Import Certificates' for operations exporting FROM Mexico; it does not ask a process question for a US operation exporting TO other countries. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.export_certificate_types_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `export_certificate_types`; not a separate CCOF question. |

| `g8_0_record_keeping.import_documentation` | Superset — CCOF's G8.0 A1 table addresses only 'Export from Mexico to the US' (the operation as Exporter of Record); it has no general import-documentation question for an operation importing FROM other countries. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.import_documentation_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `import_documentation`; not a separate CCOF question. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.import_export_records` | Superset — which import/export records are kept (certificates, contracts, phytosanitary, entry summary, labeling). G8.0's A1 table names only 'NOP Import Certificates' for the Mexico-export case; this question asks a broader record inventory CCOF does not request on this form. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.import_integrity_verification` | Superset — verifying an imported shipment had no contact with prohibited substances or ionizing radiation since export. G8.0's only import-adjacent text is the Mexico-export row's 'not treated or exposed to a prohibited substance' requirement, addressed from the exporter's side, not a general importer's. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.port_integrity_measures` | Superset — port-of-export/entry integrity measures. Not asked by G8.0; Trazo's G8.0 page C is broader than the single Mexico-export row on the grower form. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.primary_contact_records_access` | WSDA AGR 2121-O question 6. CCOF's G8.0 does not ask whether the primary contact can reach every record, nor for a backup record-holder. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.records_access_delegate` | Follow-up to `primary_contact_records_access`; see that entry. CCOF has no counterpart question. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.records_location` | WSDA AGR 2121-O question 5 asks whether all organic records are kept at the primary business location, and routes a No to their AGR 2519. CCOF's G8.0 asks nothing about WHERE records live — its Section A is the record-type table and the five-year retention attestation. Asked of every operation rather than only WSDA's, because § 205.103(c) availability is a fact about the operation, not about the certifier. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.records_maintained_as` | WSDA AGR 2121-O question 7 (electronic / hardcopy). CCOF's G8.0 does not ask what medium the records are kept in. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_company_name` | Companion detail field to uses_pest_control_company — same reasoning. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_company_notified` | Companion detail field to uses_pest_control_company — same reasoning (§205.271 notification requirement). |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation_other` | Companion detail field to preventive_measures_documentation, which the Materials Application register (ref F) already cites for the National List material-type table it maps to — this free-text "other" elaboration has no separate CCOF counterpart of its own. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.uses_pest_control_company` | §205.271 requires notifying any contracted pest control operator that the site is certified organic. CCOF's G6.2 form (the only grower form whose B3-B9 substantively maps to G9.0) does not ask whether a contracted pest control company is used as its own distinct checkbox. Trazo asks it directly as a named-company gate. |
| `materials_application.fumigant_prohibited_material_detail` | Same reason as fumigant_prohibited_material_used — it is the free-text continuation of that duplicate question, not something NOPB41 asks for. |
| `materials_application.fumigant_prohibited_material_used` | NOPB41 (the Grower Materials Application) never asks about fumigant or prohibited-material history — that disclosure belongs to the Parcel Application's land history (NOPB49 §F4/§F8) and the Affidavit of Land History. This restates the same § 205.202(b) fact a second time at the operation level rather than filling a gap CCOF's materials form leaves open. |
| `parcel_application.certified_operation_name` | Asked by OTCO C2 2.1-7 ('provide the certified operation's name and certification agency') and WSDA AGR 2264 ref 6 ('operation name'). CCOF F2 asks only whether the parcel is currently certified and §G asks for the certificate itself; the operation named on that certificate is read off the copy, never asked as a field. |
| `parcel_application.no_inputs_within_tenure` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 13 ('N/A — No input materials have been applied while under my management'). CCOF's Parcel Application asks about PROHIBITED material only (F4, the date of the last prohibited application, answered by dlpm_none_within_tenure and the land history); it never asks whether any input at all was applied. |
| `parcel_application.prior_certificate_site_number` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 6 and AGR 2262 ref 5 ('WSDA site number' / 'the site number as listed on your certificate') — WSDA's own numbering for a certified site. CCOF identifies a parcel by APN and name and prints no per-parcel number on its certificate, so its Parcel Application has nothing to ask. |
| `parcel_application.treated_lumber_contact_prevention` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.3 (how contact between existing treated lumber and organic crops or livestock is prevented). CCOF asks whether treated lumber is present and for its description and install date (Parcel Application A10 / A10a) and, on G6.0 B2, the going-forward replacement policy — never the measure that keeps installed lumber off organic crop and soil. |

### OTCO

| Question | Why it has no OTCO counterpart |
|---|---|
| `g3_0_seeds.grafts_stock` | Whether the operation grafts planting stock. No OTCO crop form asks about grafting at all — not C3, not C11 (whose category list runs fertilizers, pest and disease materials, compost and manure, inoculants, planting mixes, seed treatments, cleaners and sanitizers, adjuvants, mulches), not C7. CCOF asks it at G3.0 E1 and WSDA's §C header defines its scope as "planting or grafting stock"; OTCO's 2025 form set does not raise it. Grafting wax, tape and sealant would reach OTCO only as C11 material rows. |
| `g3_0_seeds.treatment_verification` | On what basis the seed-treatment materials are allowed (an OMRI or WSDA listing, or written certifier approval). OTCO's C3 §3.5 asks the operation to IDENTIFY its seed treatments (pelletization, coating, inoculant, fungicide, insecticide, disinfectant) and to carry them onto the C11 Crop Materials List; it never asks the allowance basis on C3, because C11 itself has a "Third Party Review Agency (OMRI / WSDA / Other)" column per material and demands a label or photo for anything not OMRI- or WSDA-listed. So OTCO answers CCOF D1's question on the materials list rather than on the seed form. CCOF asks it directly at G3.0 D1, where it is registered `covered`; the C11 register is where the OTCO-side citation belongs. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.organic_management_start_date` | When organic management of planting stock that will be SOLD as organic began — the start of the § 205.204(a)(4) twelve-month clock. C3 §3.2 asks only whether farm-grown perennial stock is used "for planting or sale" (cited at 3.2-2 through `stock_sold_as_organic`) and never follows the sale with the one-year requirement, the date, or an attestation. CCOF asks it at G3.0 A3b and WSDA at §C 4a. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_treatments` | Whether non-organic planting stock was treated before or at delivery (fungicide dip, wax, root gel). C3 §3.5 SEED TREATMENTS is scoped to seed — "Identify all seed treatments in use" — and 3.1-5's documentation question is about the inputs a CONTRACT GROWER used in production, not about a nursery's post-harvest dip on stock bought off the shelf. WSDA asks the stock case at §C 3c; CCOF and OTCO do not. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.twelve_month_attestation` | The operator's confirmation that no planting stock is sold or labelled organic before twelve months of organic management. Companion to `organic_management_start_date`; same reason — C3 stops at "for planting or sale". |
| `g4_0_rotation_soil.fertility_components` | The major components of the soil-fertility and crop-nutrient plan (crop residue, cover crops, compost, manure, mined minerals, blended or foliar fertilizers, inoculants, fertigation, rotation…). C4 has no "how do you manage soil health / fertility" checklist: its sections are tillage and erosion (4.1), rotation and in-lieu practices (4.2), manure (4.3), compost (4.4), micronutrients (4.5) and monitoring (4.6), and its § 205.203 header states the obligation without asking for an inventory of how it is met. OTCO reads the fertility INPUTS off the C11 Crop Materials List ("Intended Use: Fertility" column) and the fertility PRACTICES off 4.2–4.4. The word "fertilizer" appears on no other OTCO crop-OSP form except C9's list of materials used in NON-organic production. CCOF asks the checklist at G4.0 A2 and WSDA at §D 2, both `partial`. The field is cited in this register only as the trigger for 4.5-1 (micronutrients). |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_documentation` | Whether the operator keeps the SUPPLIER's process description or analysis for purchased compost on file — the § 205.203(c)(2) evidence for a product the certifier cannot inspect at source. C4 §4.4 routes purchased compost to C11 ("I purchase compost (and/or tea) – Provide product information in Section C11"), and C11 collects product name, manufacturer, third-party review agency and intended use, with a label or photo for anything not OMRI- or WSDA-listed; it never asks the grower to hold the composter's temperature record or lab analysis. The only OTCO document that speaks to a supplier's process is the Crop Input Verification Evaluation, which the MANUFACTURER completes ("Manure – No additives or chemical treatments used") and which otco/scope.yaml excludes as a manufacturer's own attestation. So OTCO, like CCOF (whose register unmaps this field for the same reason), leaves the supplier evidence to the materials review; WSDA alone asks it, at AGR 2196's "How you ensure compliance" column. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.purchased_compost_upload` | The attachment for `purchased_compost_documentation` above; same reason. (It would not reach a certifier in any case — `osp_module_pdf` skips `kind in ("info", "upload")`, and only parcel maps are written into the packet ZIP.) |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_frequency` | How often pest, weed and disease monitoring is performed. C5 § 5.3 has exactly one question, the monitoring METHOD, and no follow-on about frequency; a full read of the form finds "how often" only at § 5.2 ("how often burning is conducted"), which is about residue burning, not monitoring, and is cited at C5 5.2-1 (type and frequency) as the frequency Trazo does NOT capture. WSDA asks this three times (F2/G2/H2); OTCO asks it never. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_records` | How monitoring RESULTS are recorded (§ 205.201(a)(3)). C5 asks nothing about records of any kind — recordkeeping is OTCO's separate C12 Crop Recordkeeping module, which the C1 checklist routes every grower to. C5 § 5.3's one question is about the method used to judge effectiveness, and citing a records field there would be the topic-adjacent citation the second trap in ../README.md describes. WSDA F6/G5/H4 ask a records question and decline to cite this field on an axis objection; OTCO gives no occasion to decide. |
| `g5_0_pest.plastic_mulch_removal` | How plastic or synthetic mulch is removed from the field at season end (§ 205.206(c)(6)). C5's plastic-mulch question (5.1-5, "Do you use plastic mulch, landscape fabric, or other physical weed barriers?") routes a Yes to C11 — "include manufacturer and brand name on the C11 or provide a product label" — treating the barrier as a MATERIAL to be reviewed, and asks nothing about its removal. `plastic_mulch_used` is cited at 5.1-5; this follow-on is reachable only when that gate is yes and OTCO asks no question it would answer. CCOF G5.0 §A and WSDA F4/F5 both ask the removal condition and cite it. |
| `g6_0_production.drift_response_procedure` | What the operation does when it suspects drift or contact with a prohibited substance has ALREADY happened — the § 205.400(f)(1) immediate-notification duty, plus sampling, quarantine and corrective action. C9 § 9.3 asks for PREVENTION and MITIGATION plans: "describe your plan to mitigate the drift risk" (9.3-1), "describe your plan to mitigate the risk of runoff" (9.3-2), "the steps you have taken to prevent contamination from roadside management" (9.3-3). Each is about keeping the substance off the land, and each is cited against the safeguards and buffer fields. Nothing on C9 — or on C2, whose buffer table C9 points to — asks what happens after a suspected event. This is the same line wsda/unmapped/g6_0_production.yaml draws for AGR 2264 ref 14's "risk prevention strategy", and the reason the field is not cited at 9.3-1 as a topic-adjacent answer: a response procedure is not a mitigation plan, and the register should not report it as one. CCOF G6.0 A2 cites it as a Trazo-only superset beside CCOF's ten drift checkboxes because CCOF's form opens with the instruction to notify CCOF immediately of drift; C9 carries no such instruction. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.container_types` | Which containers or bins hold the product at harvest (field bins, totes, buckets, bulk trailers, lugs, single-use cartons). C7 §7.9 asks a different axis — the packaging MATERIAL in direct contact with the product (flexible plastic, glass, metal, paper, hard plastic, compostable, cardboard, twine), recorded at 7.9-1 as not covered. Citing the form-factor list there would answer a question OTCO did not ask; it is listed as the trigger instead. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.container_types_other` | Free-text elaboration of the `other` option inside Trazo's own `container_types`; same axis difference as its parent. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.custom_harvester_cleanout_verified` | Whether the custom harvester's equipment cleanout is verified before it enters organic fields. The obligation lives on OTCO's C9 §9.1 (equipment table with "describe equipment cleanout procedures to prevent contamination" and "how do you document cleaning or purging"), which is registered against C9. C7 asks about cleaning only for food contact surfaces inside a facility (§7.6). |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.custom_harvester_instructions` | How the custom-hired harvester is instructed to maintain organic integrity. No OTCO crop form asks how a hired operator is briefed; C9 §9.1 asks about the shared equipment itself. Follow-on detail for `who_harvests`, which C7 does not reach either. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.custom_harvester_records` | Which harvest records the custom harvester provides per pass. OTCO asks for harvest records on C12 §12.1 ("harvest records / field tags with field identification, date, crop name, and quantities") of every operation, regardless of who harvests — registered against C12. C7 asks for no records at all. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.who_harvests` | Who physically harvests the crop (own crew / custom-hired harvester / buyer). C7 never asks who harvests. OTCO's nearest question is C9 §9.1, which asks whether any HARVEST or transport equipment is used for both organic and non-organic crops and whether it is owned, rented, borrowed or custom-hired — a question about the equipment's exposure, not about who runs the crew, and registered against C9. |
| `g6_1_harvest_transport.who_transports` | Who moves product off the operation (own vehicles / commercial carrier / buyer pickup). C7 asks nothing about transport responsibility; C9 §9.1 asks whether TRANSPORT equipment is shared with non-organic crops (registered against C9) and C12 §12.1 asks whether shipping records and clean transport records are kept (registered against C12). |
| `g6_4_handling.custom_handling_separation` | How another grower's product is kept separate and what records are kept for their lots. Follow-on detail for `own_products_only` and unreachable without it; same boundary. C7 §7.4's commingling question looks similar and is not — it asks how ORGANIC and NON-ORGANIC crops are kept apart on shared equipment, which `commingling_controls` answers there. Keeping one grower's certified lot apart from another's is a traceability problem, not a contamination one. |
| `g6_4_handling.handling_records` | Which handling records the operation keeps (run logs, cleanout logs, drying-temperature logs, packout tickets, treatment records). C7 asks for no records; OTCO collects them on C12 §12.1, whose checklist names "post-harvest activities (washing, grading, processing, cooling/freezing, packing, etc.)" and "equipment cleaning and/or sanitation logs" — registered against C12. C7 §7.6 mentions an SOP attachment, which is a procedure, not a record, and is cited at 7.6-1 via `facility_docs`. |
| `g6_4_handling.own_products_only` | Whether the operation handles only its own crop or also product from other growers. C7 §7.3 asks about off-farm INGREDIENTS and about processing NON-ORGANIC product at the facility, never about running another grower's certified crop through the line; OTCO's C1 routes that activity to the H1 handler checklist, a handler-scope form this register does not cover. The absence is OTCO's form structure meeting our crop-scope decision. |
| `g7_0_labeling.product_leaves_as_other` | Free-text elaboration of the `other` option inside Trazo's own `product_leaves_as` checkbox group (how product leaves the operation). C8 §8.1 has its own "other (explain)" for a different axis — HOW the organic status is identified on a nonretail container — recorded at 8.1-2 as not covered. Citing this text there would answer a question OTCO did not ask. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.export_certificate_types_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `export_certificate_types`; unmapped with its parent. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.import_integrity_verification` | Verifying that an imported shipment had no contact with prohibited substances or ionizing radiation since export (§ 205.272). C12's import line asks only whether import documentation is kept (12.1-4); it does not ask how integrity is verified. WSDA asks it at §Q 5. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.port_integrity_measures` | Measures that keep organic integrity intact at the port of export or entry. Not asked on C12 or O1; WSDA asks it at §Q 5. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_company_name` | Companion detail to `uses_pest_control_company` — same reasoning. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_company_notified` | Whether the contractor has been told the site is certified organic. Companion detail to `uses_pest_control_company`; C7 §7.8 has no contractor question to hang it on. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.pest_control_records` | Which facility pest control records are kept (sighting logs, service reports, application records, device maps, corrective actions). C7 §7.8 asks for no records; OTCO's C12 §12.1 checklist ("monitoring records", "input application records that show all materials applied with date, rate and location") is where they are declared — registered against C12. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation` | How the operation documents that prevention and physical controls were insufficient before a material was applied (§ 205.271(c)). C7 §7.8 asks the adjacent question — "do pest control methods adequately prevent or control pests? if not, what other measures do you use" (7.8-5) — which is the DECISION, not its documentation. Citing the documentation checklist there would make 7.8-5 read as answered for a question it does not ask. WSDA §M 7 asks for the narrative justification itself and cites it; CCOF asks it via the Materials Application. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation_other` | Free-text elaboration of the `other` option inside Trazo's own `preventive_measures_documentation`; same reasoning as its parent. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.uses_pest_control_company` | Whether a contracted pest control company services the buildings. Read end to end, C7 §7.8 contains no question about a pest control service or contractor; OTCO's C11 Materials List catches the materials such a company applies (§7.8 twice says "all materials must be listed on the C11"), but nothing asks who applies them. Trazo asks it as the § 205.271 notification gate; the same absence is recorded for CCOF. |
| `materials_application.fumigant_prohibited_material_detail` | The substance and date behind the boolean above — its free-text continuation, reachable only when it is yes. Unmapped with the branch it belongs to; C2 § 2.4's per-year material and date columns are where OTCO asks for this detail. |
| `materials_application.fumigant_prohibited_material_used` | Whether any fumigant or other prohibited material was applied to this land in the last three years (§ 205.202(b)). C11 lists what the organic system USES going forward and never asks about past applications; OTCO asks that at C2 § 2.4 Land History — "a complete land history of all crops and applied substances for this parcel for the 36 months preceding the first planned harvest", with a Material Name / Manufacturer column and a Date Materials Applied column per year — the same place CCOF's Parcel Application (NOPB49 §F4/§F8) asks it. Trazo's own home for the fact is the Parcel Application's crop-history rows (`ParcelCropHistory.date_last_prohibited` and the substance applications), which the C2 register cites; this module's boolean restates that § 205.202(b) fact a second time at the operation level rather than answering anything C11 asks. ccof/unmapped/materials_application.yaml records the same reasoning against NOPB41. |
| `parcel_application.container_production` | Whether the parcel is container or greenhouse production. C2 asks nothing about the production system — its only nod to protected ground is the "Acres or SQ FT" unit on the crops table — and its land-history section applies to every parcel alike. OTCO routes indoor systems to a different form: the C1 Crop Activities Checklist sends "I/We grow crops in an indoor production system (Aquaponic, Container, Greenhouse)" to A1 Aqua/Container/Greenhouse, which is not a parcel_application form. CCOF asks the same yes/no on its Parcel Application (A9, F3) because it gates the land-history section there; OTCO does not gate it. |
| `parcel_application.livestock_detail` | The livestock and manure-management description shown when `livestock_present` is yes. Same reason: neither C2 nor FACT-04 asks about livestock on a crop parcel. Manure APPLIED to the parcel is a different question — it is a material in C2's 2.4 land-history table (Material Name / Manufacturer, example "Chicken Manure / On-farm"), cited at C2 2.4-8. |
| `parcel_application.livestock_present` | Whether livestock is kept on the parcel. C2 has no livestock section and FACT-04 lists pasture as a CROP with acreage ("Pasture (60 acres)"), not as livestock use. CCOF puts §C livestock on its Parcel Application because one form serves crop and livestock parcels; OTCO's crop OSP set (O1, OFPP, A1, C1–C14, W1, IS, FACT-04, Land Transfer) contains no livestock form, and its C1 checklist routes crop activities only — a grazier files OTCO's separate livestock OSP. |
| `parcel_application.no_inputs_within_tenure` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 13 ('N/A — No input materials have been applied while under my management'). OTCO's C2 land history asks for the materials applied and the last prohibited application, not for a statement that no input of any kind was applied. |
| `parcel_application.prior_certificate_site_number` | Asked by WSDA AGR 2264 ref 6 and AGR 2262 ref 5 — WSDA assigns each certified site its own number. OTCO C2 2.1-7 asks for the certified operation's name and agency and 2.4-2 for a copy of the certificate; the field or parcel is identified by name and APN on the certificate, not by a certifier-assigned site number. |

### WSDA

| Question | Why it has no WSDA counterpart |
|---|---|
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_areas` | Which risk areas describe the operation — split production, uncertified suppliers, supplier churn, complex chains, custom operators, seasonal labour, imports. §P never asks the operation to characterise its own vulnerability. It goes straight to controls, and its one risk-adjacent option, `vulnerability_assessment`, appears inside Trazo's mitigation list rather than WSDA's. The nearest WSDA question, §P 5, asks how SUPPLIERS are evaluated and approved, which is one risk area treated as a procedure. CCOF asks the risk-area checklist at G8.0 D1. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.fraud_risk_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `fraud_risk_areas`; unmapped with its parent. §P has no risk-area list to carry an `other`. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_review_frequency` | When the plan itself is reviewed and updated — annually, on change, before inspection. §P asks how the plan is IMPLEMENTED (ref 2) and whether internal audits happen (ref 3), and WSDA runs a LIVING plan: a renewing operation updates the sections that changed rather than re-filing, so the form has no reason to ask for a review cadence the way an annual re-filing would. It is `triggered_by` on §P 3, where it indicates the section applies, but it does not answer it. CCOF asks the cadence directly on the Certification Contract, ref B2. |
| `g2_0_fraud_prevention.osp_review_frequency_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `osp_review_frequency`; unmapped with its parent. |
| `g3_2_planting_stock.stock_types_established` | Which propagation forms were established (bare-root, containerized, rootstock, cuttings/scions, crowns/divisions). WSDA's §C header DEFINES these forms — "any plant or plant tissue other than annual seedlings but including rhizomes, shoots, leaf or stem cuttings, roots, or tubers" — to set the section's scope, and then never asks which of them the operation uses. §C ref 1 asks acquisition SOURCE (nursery / own / contract / other), which is a different axis and is answered by `planting_stock_description` there. Citing this field against ref 1 would report propagation form as though it were source. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.compost_initial_cn_ratio` | The initial carbon:nitrogen ratio of the feedstock, which § 205.203(c)(2) fixes between 25:1 and 40:1 as the precondition for the temperature window that follows. WSDA's §D 9a asks only for the OUTCOME and its evidence — how the pile is mixed and managed so all feedstocks reach 131°F (55°C) for at least three days, and what records demonstrate it — and never asks for the ratio that made that outcome achievable. §D 8 asks which feedstocks are used, by category (manure or other animal materials / plant materials / newspaper or other recycled paper / other), not in any proportion from which a ratio could be read. CCOF's G4.1 A2b does ask for the number. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_source` | Asked by OTCO C4 §4.3 (is the manure purchased or produced off-farm). WSDA §D asks whether raw manure is applied and how the interval and water-protection rules are met, never where the manure comes from. |
| `g4_1_compost_manure.raw_manure_supplier_statement` | Asked by OTCO C4 §4.3 (label or supplier statement that purchased manure is untreated). WSDA's forms ask for no manure-provenance document; the material's listing is judged on AGR 2196 instead. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.conservation_plan_agency` | Whether a current conservation plan or agreement with an agency or programme exists (NRCS, RCD, a state programme). WSDA's §E asks which NRCS PRACTICES are used but never whether the operation is enrolled in a plan or programme with the agency those practices come from — the practice vocabulary is borrowed, the relationship is not asked about. CCOF asks it directly at G4.2 A2, where it is registered `covered`. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.conservation_plan_detail` | The agency or programme name and what its plan covers. Follow-on detail for `conservation_plan_agency` above; the same reasoning applies, and there is no §E question it could attach to. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.irrigation_district_additives` | Whether the district adds substances prohibited in organic production. Same gate as `water_from_irrigation_district` above — E8 asks what the OPERATION injects, never what arrives already in the water. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.irrigation_district_documentation` | The district's written statement or treatment schedule. The attachment for `irrigation_district_mitigation`; no §E question calls for it. (It would not reach a certifier in any case — `osp_module_pdf` skips `kind in ("info", "upload")`, and only parcel maps are written into the packet ZIP.) |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.irrigation_district_mitigation` | How the operation monitors for those substances and keeps them off its fields. E8b does ask for "practices to prevent contamination of certified crops", but only of an operation that answered yes to applying its own input materials through the irrigation system; an operation receiving treated district water reaches that question by no path at all. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.monitoring_method` | How natural-resource OUTCOMES are monitored across the operation (observation, records, formal assessment). §E's only monitoring question, E10, asks a narrower thing — which activities ensure irrigation water is used efficiently, offering soil moisture sensors, visual observations and scheduling software. Citing this field there would answer outcome-monitoring generally while leaving E10's actual ask, irrigation efficiency, unanswered and looking covered. CCOF asks the general version at G4.2 B1. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.monitoring_method_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `monitoring_method`; unmapped for the same reason as its parent. E10 does offer its own "Other", but it is an "other irrigation efficiency monitoring activity", not an other outcome-monitoring method. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.water_from_irrigation_district` | Whether any irrigation water arrives through an irrigation district or other shared delivery system. WSDA's nearest question, E8, is gated on "Do you apply input materials THROUGH YOUR IRRIGATION SYSTEM" — the operation's own chemigation. A district chlorinating or treating shared canal water triggers nothing in §E, because the operation applies nothing. CCOF asks the district case directly at G6.0 D3, which is a California-shaped question: shared surface-water districts are the normal delivery mechanism there. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.water_quality_test_frequency` | How often that testing happens. Follow-on detail for `water_quality_tested`; same reasoning. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.water_quality_tested` | Whether irrigation water quality is tested. §E asks about water quality only as PRACTICES that maintain or improve it against three named contaminant classes (E13 nutrients, E15 pesticides, E17 sedimentation) and never asks whether the water is sampled. E10, the one monitoring question in the section, is scoped to irrigation EFFICIENCY. CCOF does not ask this either — it is in ccof/unmapped for the same reason. |
| `g4_2_natural_resources.wildlife_habitat_pressure` | Whether the operation removes or degrades wildlife habitat (land clearing, hedgerow removal), which is the trigger for the mitigation question that follows it. WSDA asks for biodiversity PRACTICES unconditionally at E2 and never establishes a pressure that would require offsetting; its only two conditional facts, E4 (permanent ground cover ≥ 90%) and E5 (slope < 10%), are erosion-risk skip logic, not habitat pressure. So the mitigation field has a home at E2 while its own trigger has none — CCOF asks the pair at A4 and A7. |
| `g5_0_pest.burn_crops` | Which crops or residues are burned. Follow-on detail for `burns_crop_residue`; unmapped for the same reason, and reachable only when that gate is yes. |
| `g5_0_pest.burn_reason` | Why it is burned — the § 205.203(e) exception being relied on. Follow-on detail for `burns_crop_residue`; same reason. CCOF asks it at G5.0 C3. |
| `g5_0_pest.burn_reason_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `burn_reason`; unmapped with the branch it belongs to. |
| `g5_0_pest.burns_crop_residue` | Whether crop residue is burned. § 205.203(e) bars burning crop residues except to suppress disease or stimulate seed germination, and CCOF asks the whole branch (G5.0 §A burning gate, C2 which crops, C3 why). None of WSDA's three pest sections raises burning at all: §F's preventive list offers "Flame weeding", which is in-row thermal weed control rather than residue burning, and §H's offers "Field sanitation (physical removal)", which names physical removal precisely to distinguish it. §D (soil fertility) does not ask either. |
| `g5_0_pest.monitoring_records` | How monitoring RESULTS are recorded. WSDA asks a records question three times — F6, G5 and H4, "describe the records you maintain regarding your preventative weed / pest / disease management" — and all three are about the records documenting the PREVENTATIVE PRACTICES, not about monitoring output. The distinction is the whole point of those rows: WSDA has already asked how effectiveness is monitored (F1/G1/H1) and how often (F2/G2/H2), and then asks separately what paperwork the prevention leaves behind. Citing this field there would report monitoring-result recordkeeping as though it answered practice recordkeeping, and those rows would stop showing as the gaps they are. |
| `g6_0_production.drift_response_procedure` | What the operation does when it suspects drift or contact with a prohibited substance has already happened. AGR 2264 ref 14 asks for the "risk prevention strategy" per border, which is prevention; the field cited there covers that half. No WSDA question asks for the RESPONSE — the sampling, quarantine and notification steps after a suspected event. The nearest is §P 6, criteria for reporting suspected organic FRAUD to the WSDA Organic Program or the USDA National Organic Program, which is a different event with a different duty. |
| `g6_0_production.nonorganic_system_materials` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.4 (a list of materials used in the non-organic production system). WSDA's split-operation questions ask how organic and non-organic product are kept apart and how prohibited materials are stored, never for the conventional side's own materials list. |
| `g6_0_production.parallel_production` | Whether the SAME crop or variety is grown under both organic and conventional management — the § 205.201(a)(5) parallel-production case, which is stricter than a split operation because two indistinguishable lots exist at harvest. WSDA asks the split question (§I 2, equipment used on both certified and non-certified crops; §L 3, post-harvest handling of both) and never narrows it to the same crop or variety. A keyword sweep of all 24 registered WSDA forms finds "parallel" only in §B's header definition of an annual seedling. CCOF asks it at G8.0 C1. |
| `g6_0_production.parallel_production_distinction` | How organic and conventional lots of the same crop are told apart at harvest and sale. Follow-on detail for `parallel_production`, and unreachable without it. WSDA asks adjacent questions — §J 12/12a, whether certified and non-certified crops share a transport unit and how they are segregated; §L 3a, how they are kept separate in post-harvest handling — but both are about physical separation of DIFFERENT products, never about distinguishing two lots of the same variety, which is the case that cannot be solved by separation alone. |
| `g6_0_production.prohibited_materials_on_site` | Whether any materials prohibited in organic production are kept anywhere on the operation. WSDA's crop OSP asks what materials are USED (AGR 2196 Input Material List) and what equipment is shared (§I), never what is stored on site unused. A keyword sweep across all 24 registered forms returns no storage-of-prohibited-materials question at any ref. CCOF asks it at G6.0 E1, and the storage arrangement at E2 — where it is one of the few `covered` rows in that register. |
| `g6_0_production.prohibited_materials_storage` | How those materials are stored and kept away from organic product, inputs and equipment. Follow-on detail for `prohibited_materials_on_site`; same reason. §M (Facility Pest Management) covers pest-control materials in storage and post-harvest areas, which is a different set and a different risk. |
| `g6_0_production.prohibited_materials_storage_other` | Free-text elaboration for the `other` option inside `prohibited_materials_storage`; unmapped with the branch it belongs to. |
| `g6_0_production.runoff_mitigation_plan` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.3 (the runoff mitigation plan). Follows the runoff-risk question above, which this certifier does not ask. |
| `g6_0_production.runoff_risk_present` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.3 (risk of runoff carrying prohibited materials onto organic land). WSDA asks about drift and about buffers per border; water-borne contamination from neighbouring land is not a separate question. |
| `g6_4_handling.custom_handling_separation` | How another grower's product is kept separate, and what records are kept for their lots. Follow-on detail for `own_products_only` and unreachable without it; same boundary. §L 3a asks a question that looks similar and is not — how CERTIFIED and NON-CERTIFIED crops are kept separate, which is the split-operation case and is answered by `commingling_controls` there. Keeping one grower's certified lot apart from another's is a traceability problem, not a contamination one. |
| `g6_4_handling.handling_site` | A description of the buildings, pads or equipment used for handling. §L asks in detail about the handling PROCESS — activities, cleaning methods, sanitizers, water source and treatment, packaging — and never about the premises it happens in. WSDA collects facility detail on the Additional Facilities and Third-Parties form (AGR 2519), which `wsda/scope.yaml` records as a gap rather than a decision: §J 13, §K 1 and §L 1 all route a grower to it and Trazo does not generate it. So this is a field with a WSDA home that this register does not yet reach, not a field WSDA has no use for. ⛔ It was briefly cited against §L 2 and withdrawn: L2 asks whether handling happens at the farm at all, and `handling_site` describes where — close enough to look right, and it made the row read `covered` for a question it does not answer. `cross_certifier_conflicts` caught it against CCOF's G6.4 A1 (`not_covered`, because A1 asks for a formal site NAME and ADDRESS that no field holds). |
| `g6_4_handling.own_products_only` | Whether the operation handles only its own crop or also product from other growers. WSDA asks this of handlers, on the Handler OSP (AGR 2180), which wsda/scope.yaml excludes. §L is the crop-producer section and assumes throughout that the crop being handled is the operation's own — its only third-party question, ref 1, runs the other way (does a third party handle YOUR crops). So the absence here is our scope decision meeting WSDA's form structure, not a question WSDA neglects to ask. |
| `g6_4_handling.products_handled` | Which crops and product forms are handled at the site. §L establishes THAT the operation handles its own crop after harvest (ref 2) and then asks how — cleaning, water, sanitizers, packaging — without ever asking which crops go through it. It does not need to: for a crop producer the answer is the crops on the site applications, which WSDA already holds from AGR 2264 ref 8 and ref 10. The question earns its place in Trazo because a handling line that runs some crops and not others is a real distinction; it is not one WSDA asks a crop producer to draw. |
| `g7_0_labeling.label_has_usda_seal` | Whether the USDA organic seal appears on the label. WSDA reviews the seal when the label copy is submitted for approval under §N ref 5, and never asks about it as a separate question on the OSP. |
| `g7_0_labeling.label_states_certifier` | Whether the consumer label carries 'Certified organic by [agent]'. §N ref 7 asks something narrower and different: whether any label names an agency OTHER than WSDA below the distributor information, and how often updated certificates are requested to keep that displayed distributor verified. Citing this Trazo boolean there would answer the presence question while leaving ref 7's actual ask — the re-verification cadence — unanswered and looking covered. |
| `g7_0_labeling.organic_label_categories` | § 205.301 labeling-category tier (100% organic / organic / made with organic). WSDA's crop-producer §N never asks which tier an operation sells under; the tier is asked on the handler-side product applications (AGR 2523 / 2524), which wsda/scope.yaml excludes as handler certification scope. The absence here is a fact about §N's audience, not about WSDA's forms as a whole. |
| `g7_0_labeling.product_leaves_as_other` | Free-text elaboration of the `other` option inside Trazo's own `product_leaves_as` checkbox group. WSDA §N ref 1 has its own `other` for container TYPE — produce boxes, totes, bulk trailers, grain elevators — which ref 1's gap already records as uncaptured. Trazo's `other` describes a different axis (how product leaves), so citing it against ref 1 would answer a question WSDA did not ask. |
| `g8_0_record_keeping.export_certificate_process` | How export certificates are requested, verified and kept. §Q asks WHICH documents accompany each shipment (ref 9) and which certificates the destination requires (ref 7), and it asks the process question only on the IMPORT side, at ref 5 — how imported seed is verified not to have been treated or irradiated, with the records maintained. There is no export-side equivalent: WSDA takes the document list as the answer and does not ask how the operation obtains or retains those certificates. CCOF does not ask it either. |
| `g9_0_facility_pest.preventive_measures_documentation_other` | Free-text elaboration of the `other` option inside Trazo's own `preventive_measures_documentation` checkbox group. WSDA §M asks for the narrative justification itself (why prevention was insufficient before a material was applied), not for a category-plus-other breakdown of how that was documented, so there is no WSDA question this free text answers. |
| `materials_application.fertilizers_none_used` | CCOF NOPB41 Header C's per-section N/A, asked per category. AGR 2196 has no category sections and no N/A — one flat table. |
| `materials_application.no_materials_used` | OTCO C11 11.1 (not applicable) ('Not Applicable; no materials/inputs are used') and CCOF NOPB41 Header C (mark a section 'Not applicable'). AGR 2196 is a list to be completed, with no N/A checkbox: WSDA's header says every crop producer files it, and an operation using nothing files an empty list. The statement compiles into the narrative WSDA reads either way. |
| `materials_application.pest_disease_weed_none_used` | Same as fertilizers_none_used: CCOF's per-section N/A; AGR 2196 is one flat table without sections. |
| `materials_application.post_harvest_contact_none_used` | Same as fertilizers_none_used: CCOF's per-section N/A; AGR 2196 is one flat table without sections. |
| `materials_application.production_aids_none_used` | Same as fertilizers_none_used: CCOF's per-section N/A; AGR 2196 is one flat table without sections. |
| `parcel_application.apn` | The assessor's parcel number. WSDA identifies a site by name plus location, and its location ask (AGR 2264 ref 2) enumerates street address, city, state, zip, county, Township/Range/ Section and GPS coordinates — the PLSS description, which is the survey system in use across Washington. It never asks for a county assessor's parcel number. CCOF's Parcel Application does, because an APN is how a California county identifies a parcel of record. |
| `parcel_application.container_production` | Whether the parcel is container or greenhouse production. WSDA's crop OSP has no container or greenhouse section at all: AGR 2264's own header defines a site as "a distinct field, orchard, block, pasture, circle, or other contiguous area", and the only enclosed-production section in AGR 2121 is §S, which is scoped to fungi. CCOF asks it on the Parcel Application and follows up with a whole form, G3.1 Container and Greenhouse Production. An operation growing under cover in Washington is answering a different application than this register compares. |
| `parcel_application.dlpm_none_within_tenure` | The operator's declaration that no PROHIBITED material was applied since it began managing the parcel. WSDA does not ask for that declaration. Its N/A on AGR 2264 ref 13 states that no input material of any kind was applied, which is a different statement; until 2026-09-30 the register cited this declaration there (OSP alignment audit 2026-10, T17). WSDA's land history is the dated list of inputs itself, which ref 13 maps to the land-history years. |
| `parcel_application.no_lapse_attested` | Asked by CCOF Parcel Application §G(2) ('verification of no lapse in organic management') and OTCO C2 2.4-2 ('verification there has been no lapse in organic management'). WSDA AGR 2264 ref 6 asks whether the site is or was certified within 36 months and for the previous certificate and a signed AGR 2262; it never asks for a continuity statement, because a WSDA-to-WSDA site transfer is verified against WSDA's own records. |
| `parcel_application.transition_card` | A display of what Trazo's records show about the 36-month window, not an answer. WSDA's nearest question, AGR 2264 ref 4, asks which status the operator is APPLYING for (organic or transitional); no question asks that yet, and the card is not the operator's application. |
| `parcel_application.treated_lumber_contact_prevention` | Asked by OTCO C9 §9.3 (how contact between existing treated lumber and organic crops or livestock is prevented). WSDA 2264 ref 12 asks whether treated wood is located in a manner that contacts soil, plants or livestock, and 12a when it was installed — never how contact is prevented. |
| `w2_0_wild_crop.wild_crop_upload` | WSDA's Wild Harvest section (R) asks only for narrative descriptions of the harvest area, methods, and monitoring — no question requests a site map or landowner statement attachment the way this optional upload offers. |
